Its developer program spans three surfaces: the Double 3 SDK (a local command-and-event API exposed over a Unix domain socket on the robot, covering base movement, navigation, PTZ cameras, depth sensors, WebRTC calling, and standby/sidebar apps), iOS SDKs for the Double 2 (Basic Control and Camera Kit), and a Fleet REST API for programmatic access to fleet-management data such as robots, users, call logs, and visitor passes. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched against the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Ubitricity
providers.description: Ubitricity is a Berlin-based electric vehicle charging company and wholly-owned subsidiary of Shell, best known for integrating EV charge points into existing street infrastructure such as lampposts and bollards. It operates the UK's largest public on-street charging network, with further networks in Germany and France, providing charge point hardware (Simple Socket lamppost units, AC and DC chargers), a managed charging platform built on the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), and Pay-As-You-Go driver charging. The company does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Zeew
providers.description: Zeew is a European (Estonia-based) white-label, no-code delivery-platform provider that lets businesses launch on-demand delivery marketplaces and apps in days. Its platform powers food, grocery, pharmacy, retail, and home-services delivery with connected customer, vendor, and driver apps plus an admin dashboard, sold as SaaS subscriptions or purchasable source code under a reseller / white-labeling program. Zeew runs a backend API host (api.zeew.eu) that serves its white-label apps, but as of mid-2026 publishes no public, self-serve API reference, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or webhook catalog; integration is delivered through the managed platform. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Ascend Elements
providers.description: Ascend Elements is a Westborough, Massachusetts battery materials company that manufactures engineered lithium-ion battery materials from valuable elements reclaimed from spent lithium-ion batteries and gigafactory manufacturing scrap. Founded in 2015 as Battery Resourcers out of MIT-affiliated research by Eric Gratz and Professor Yan Wang, it recovers up to 98% of the critical battery metals in end-of-life cells and uses its patented Hydro-to-Cathode direct cathode precursor (pCAM) synthesis process to produce cathode precursor and battery-grade lithium carbonate, reducing the carbon footprint of new EV battery cathode material by up to 90%. Its Base 1 facility in Covington, Georgia is North America's largest electric-vehicle battery recycling plant, and Apex 1 in Hopkinsville, Kentucky is its commercial pCAM plant. Ascend Elements publishes no public developer API for its materials, recycling or logistics business; the only machine-readable surface observed on its own hosts is the WordPress REST API at ascendelements.com/wp-json, which serves the corporate website's content, media-coverage, jobs and supplier sourcing-event collections.

providers.name: Portside
providers.description: Portside is a cloud-based business aviation management software company headquartered in Cary, North Carolina, serving corporate flight departments, charter and managed fleets, fractional and aircraft management companies, business jet owners, and government and military aviation across more than 30 countries. The Portside Platform is a suite of modular applications spanning scheduling and flight operations, fleet and crew optimization, a crew staffing marketplace, managed-aircraft customer billing, aviation reporting and analytics, an aircraft owner portal, a Safety Management System (SMS), RiskAssist flight risk assessment, and hotel and car reservations. Portside integrates with a wide range of business aviation systems across scheduling, charter marketplaces, accounting, maintenance, expense management, CRM, payments, trip services, fuel management, and risk/safety, but does not publish a public developer API or self-service developer portal; integrations are arranged directly with the Portside team. Portside is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Vanderhall Motor Works
providers.description: Vanderhall Motor Works is a privately held American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2010 by Steve Hall and headquartered in Provo, Utah. The company hand-builds three-wheeled autocycles — the Laguna, Venice, Venice Speedster, Carmel and Santarosa — alongside the all-electric Edison and the quad-motor Brawley off-road UTV, selling through an independent dealer network rather than direct to consumers. Its software footprint is internal rather than commercial: Vanderhall runs a dealer portal, an admin portal and a parts/accessory shop on its own domain, and the admin portal publishes an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at https://portal.vanderhallusa.com/mcp with RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata and RFC 7591 dynamic client registration. There is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and no public API reference.

providers.name: Replica
providers.description: Replica is a San Francisco-based data platform for the built environment, spun out of Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs in 2019, that operates a nationwide activity-based travel model. Its analytical engine combines public data (US Census/ACS, GTFS transit feeds, OpenStreetMap road networks, land-use records, state traffic counts) with licensed private data (de-identified aggregate mobile location, credit transaction and driving-behavior data) to synthesize a privacy-preserving simulated population and a complete trip table for the United States. Products include Places (seasonal, high-fidelity activity-based travel model), Trends (weekly near-real-time mobility and land-use data), Safety Hub, Safe Streets Planner, and a suite of workflow applications used by state DOTs, MPOs, transit agencies, cities and counties. Data is consumed through the Replica Studio web platform, CSV export and direct database access; Replica publishes documented dataset schemas at documentation.replicahq.com but no public developer REST API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Carrier Global
providers.description: Carrier Global Corporation is a global provider of healthy, safe, sustainable, and intelligent building and cold-chain solutions, spanning HVAC, refrigeration, fire, security, and building automation technologies. Its digital ecosystem includes the Lynx Fleet telematics platform (Lynx APIs for transport refrigeration units), the Abound building management platform, i-Vu and Carrier Comfort Network for commercial building automation, and the Carrier SmartHome app for residential smart thermostats.

providers.name: Platform Science
providers.description: Platform Science is an enterprise connected-vehicle and fleet management platform for commercial trucking and transportation. It combines ELD and telematics, driver applications (Hours of Service, DVIR, navigation, workflow, media management), back-office fleet management, and video safety intelligence on a single connected-vehicle platform. Its Virtual Vehicle Marketplace hosts 100+ partner integrations across 18 categories (asset tracking, compliance, fuel, navigation, sensors, TMS, and more), and a gated developer program (the Remote Platform Management system, an Android SDK, and a data-retrieval API governed by SPEED Certification) lets partners build edge and cloud integrations against the platform.

providers.name: Autofleet
providers.description: Autofleet is a fleet and mobility optimization platform founded in 2018 in Tel Aviv by Kobi Eisenberg and Dor Shay, and since 2024 an independently operated, wholly owned subsidiary of Element Fleet Management Corp. (TSX: EFN). Its AI-driven software plans, dispatches, routes and simulates vehicle-based operations across postal and parcel delivery, last-mile logistics, rental and car sharing, corporate motor pools, microtransit, NEMT and school transport, taxi and rideshare, field service, and autonomous mobility, in more than 20 countries. The platform is sold as an integration hub — Autofleet markets a public API and webhooks for connecting telematics, GPS, keyless access, maintenance, booking, dispatch, CRM and ERP systems — and adds Nova, a fleet-specific generative AI layer for natural-language operational questions. The API gateway is live at api.autofleet.io, but the developer reference at docs.autofleet.io is a password-protected ReadMe hub, so no machine-readable contract is publicly retrievable.

providers.name: Firefly
providers.description: Firefly Systems Inc. is a data-first moving out-of-home (mOOH) advertising network that turns taxis, rideshare vehicles, and other mobility assets into digital and static advertising surfaces across 15+ major North American markets and several countries. Its network of tens of thousands of GPS-connected screens delivers geo-targeted, contextual, and programmatic digital out-of-home (DOOH) campaigns with advanced tracking, attribution, and measurement. Firefly offers digital and static car tops, full and partial car wraps, in-car TaxiTV, around-car activations, and experiential LED and hologram truck formats. Programmatic demand reaches Firefly inventory through third-party DOOH supply-side platforms rather than a Firefly endpoint — its own advertising-solutions page names Place Exchange, Vistar Media, Hivestack and Broadsign, alongside a VIOOH integration, and supports Programmatic Guaranteed and open-marketplace deals. The company is backed by investors including 500 Global, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and GV (Google Ventures).

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: JOLT
providers.description: JOLT is a Sydney-headquartered electric vehicle charging network operator that builds and runs free-to-start kerbside DC fast chargers across Australia, and has since extended the same model into New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its charge points deliver the first 7kWh of each day's charging at no cost — around 45km of range in roughly 15 minutes over CCS2 or CHAdeMO — funded not by the driver but by the digital out-of-home advertising screens mounted on the charger itself, which makes JOLT simultaneously a charge point operator and a media network selling audience reach to advertisers. It sits in the energy value chain as a downstream infrastructure and demand-side player: it buys electricity (claiming 100% GreenPower green-certified wind and solar), owns and operates the charging assets on public and retail land in partnership with governments and hosts such as Transport for NSW, Ausgrid and major grocery retailers, and monetises the dwell time rather than the kilowatt-hour. Its API posture is honestly closed. JOLT publishes no developer programme, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no open data feed; the only public HTTP surfaces on its domains are a marketing WordPress install (whose custom jolt/v1 REST namespace exposes a single VAT form endpoint) and an api.joltcharge.com host that serves a static redirect to the mobile app rather than any API. It is not a designated data holder under the Australian Consumer Data Right for energy — it does not appear in the CDR Register's energy data holder brands — so the CDR energy mandate that compels Australian electricity retailers to expose standardised usage and tariff data does not reach it, and no OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118 or Green Button/ESPI conformance is published. All customer charging data, session history and audience analytics are reachable only through the JOLT consumer app or a sales conversation.

providers.name: Poplin
providers.description: Poplin (formerly SudShare) is a nationwide on-demand laundry pickup and delivery marketplace connecting customers with independent, work-from-home "Laundry Pros" who wash, dry, and fold laundry, serving 500+ cities and 150,000+ customers. Poplin operates two consumer-facing mobile apps - the customer app and the Laundry Pro app - plus a Laundry Pro web portal (laundry-pro.poplin.co), but it does not expose a public or partner developer API. No developer portal or API reference was found at poplin.co, and the api.poplin.co subdomain resolves but returns a bare 404 with no documentation, indicating internal-only use. Business/SMB accounts (property managers, hospitality) are onboarded through sales and an account manager rather than through self-service API keys.

providers.name: Twaice
providers.description: TWAICE (TWAICE Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based battery analytics software company. Its predictive analytics platform turns BMS data from battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric-vehicle fleets into actionable insights for performance management, warranty management, safety monitoring, digital commissioning, and BESS reporting, alongside a battery simulation model library for engineers. Customers include BESS asset owners and operators, IPPs, utilities, automotive and bus/truck OEMs, and battery manufacturers. TWAICE is ISO 27001 certified, holds the automotive TISAX label, and is backed by investors including Creandum and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API or developer program; the platform is a closed SaaS.

providers.name: ChowNow
providers.description: ChowNow is a Playa Vista, Los Angeles-based restaurant technology company providing commission-free online ordering, branded mobile apps, marketing tools, and operational software purpose-built for independent restaurants. Founded in 2011, ChowNow powers ordering websites, native iOS/Android apps, QR-code dine-in ordering, catering, email and SMS marketing, a rewards program, Flex Delivery, order aggregation, and centralized menu management for 20,000+ restaurants. The platform integrates with 20+ point-of-sale systems including Toast, Square, Revel, Clover, Lightspeed, Heartland Genius, Skytab, and PosiTouch, and syndicates restaurant menus through a Discovery Network spanning Google, Apple Maps, Yelp, and other channels, with optional hand-off to DoorDash, UberEats, and Grubhub for last-mile delivery. ChowNow's business model is flat-fee software-as-a-service for restaurants rather than per-order commissions, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks reference, or open developer portal. Third-party integration is handled through pre-built connectors managed inside the restaurant dashboard and a private partnerships program; prospective POS, delivery, and technology partners apply through a partnerships form rather than self-serve API documentation. The company's public GitHub presence consists primarily of forks of open-source Python/JavaScript tooling and archived internal libraries, with no SDK, client library, or specification repositories.

providers.name: Cleanly
providers.description: Cleanly was a US-based on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning startup (backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator) that has since rebranded and now operates as ByNext at bynext.co. ByNext is an app-based, on-demand laundry, dry cleaning, and home cleaning pickup and delivery service operating 7 days a week (8am-8pm) with 24-48 hour turnaround across metro markets including New York City, New Jersey, the Washington D.C. area, and Los Angeles. Booking is handled through its iOS and Android apps with real-time driver tracking, pay-per-pound or subscription pricing, and free pickup and delivery. Cleanly/ByNext exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public web and consumer-app footprint. The original cleanly.com domain now redirects to bynext.co.

providers.name: Nauto
providers.description: Nauto is a predictive AI platform for commercial fleet safety. Using in-vehicle AI dash cams and computer vision, it monitors driver behavior in real time, delivers predictive collision alerts before incidents occur, scores driver risk with its VERA system, and powers driver coaching, exoneration, and incident intelligence. Nauto also supports DVIR, IFTA, and ELD fleet-compliance workflows across trucking, delivery, construction, passenger transit, and field-service fleets. Backed by Greylock, Playground Global, and SoftBank Vision Fund, Nauto is SOC 2 Type 1/2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified.

providers.name: Omnitracs
providers.description: Omnitracs is a commercial fleet management, telematics, and transportation-management provider, now part of Solera Inc. (acquired 2021, operating under Solera Fleet Solutions). Its Omnitracs One platform and the Omnitracs Roadnet routing platform serve roughly 15,000 fleet customers with ELD / Hours-of-Service compliance, telematics and GPS positioning, driver workflow and messaging, routing and dispatch, and video safety. Omnitracs exposes real integration APIs and web services (Roadnet Web Services, the Services Portal Entity Management web services, and the SOAP/XML Event Subscription Service that streams positions, messages, HOS, and critical events), but access is partner- and customer-account gated - there is no open, self-service public developer portal. API credentials (a username/password with API access) and the integration developer wiki are provisioned to contracted customers and integration partners. Endpoints documented here for gated surfaces are honestly modeled from public integration notes, not from an open reference.

providers.name: Skootar
providers.description: Skootar is a Thai on-demand courier, messenger, and logistics platform serving Bangkok, its surrounding provinces, and Chonburi. It offers same-day document delivery, cheque and bill collection, parcel shipping, business food delivery, and on-demand pickup-truck and moving jobs across a fleet of motorcycles, cars, and trucks, all with real-time tracking. Orders can be placed 24/7 through the website, the mobile app, or an API intended for high-volume businesses to wire delivery ordering into their own back-office systems. Skootar reports more than 130,000 business customers, 26,000+ drivers, and 9.2 million+ completed deliveries over 12 years, and is backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published; API access is arranged through its business/enterprise channel.

providers.name: Flexitricity
providers.description: Flexitricity Limited is an Edinburgh-based energy flexibility aggregator and licensed electricity supplier operating what it describes as the first, largest and most advanced demand response portfolio in Great Britain — a virtual power plant exceeding 1GW. Founded in 2004 by Dr Alastair Martin, acquired by Alpiq in 2014, merged with Quinbrook's Velox Power in 2022, and per the company's own timeline acquired by Drax in 2026, it sits in the value chain between commercial, industrial and aggregated domestic energy assets and the GB wholesale and balancing markets. It routes customer assets — batteries, standby generation, industrial load, hydrogen electrolysers, co-located sites and, through its FlexGO product, residential EV charging — into the Balancing Mechanism, Capacity Market, frequency response, reserve services, the Demand Flexibility Service, DNO flexibility markets and wholesale trading. Its API posture is closed: Flexitricity publishes no developer portal, no documented public API, no OpenAPI, and no open market data of its own. The developer-facing subdomains developer., developers., docs., api. and data. do not resolve; the only interactive surface is portal.flexitricity.com, which requires a customer account. The United Kingdom has no consumer data-portability mandate comparable to Australia's Consumer Data Right, so nothing compels Flexitricity to expose customer usage data through an API. The open, machine-readable data about Flexitricity is published by Elexon, not by Flexitricity — its 63 registered BM Units under lead party FLEXTRCY are retrievable anonymously from the Elexon BMRS Insights API. Open on the regulator's side, closed on its own: that split is the finding.

providers.name: Kiwibot
providers.description: Kiwibot — legally Kiwi Campus, Inc., and rebranded to Robot.com in October 2025 — builds and operates fleets of autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, warehouse logistics robots, quadruped and humanoid platforms, and robot-mounted advertising units. Founded in Berkeley, California in 2017 by Felipe Chavez and Jason Oviedo out of a UC Berkeley campus food-delivery pilot, the company reports more than 1.7 million completed real-world autonomous tasks for campus dining, retail, grocery and enterprise customers across the United States, Canada, Colombia, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, and acquired mobile-advertising firm Nickelytics in 2023. Its B2B delivery platform is exposed as an API-key-gated REST service on a Google Cloud Endpoints gateway at api.kiwibot.com — historically integrated by ordering partners such as Shopify and Ordermark — but the company publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract; access runs through the sales/demo form. Its autonomy team publishes substantial first-party open source ROS 2 tooling from the github.com/kiwicampus organization.

providers.name: NoScrubs
providers.description: NoScrubs (NoScrubs, Inc., dba NoScrubs Laundry Delivery) is an on-demand wash-and-fold laundry pickup and delivery service operating across US metros including the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Dallas-Fort Worth, Miami, Phoenix, Austin, and Houston. Customers schedule a pickup through the NoScrubs mobile app or website; trained laundry professionals ("Scrubbers") collect laundry from the doorstep within a two-hour window, professionally wash, dry, and fold it using hypoallergenic unscented detergents, and return it the same day in as little as four hours. NoScrubs also offers monthly subscription plans, gift cards, and a wash-and-fold service for businesses. It is a consumer service company with no public developer API; the site publishes an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: Benchmark Minerals
providers.description: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence is the world's leading market intelligence and price reporting agency for the lithium-ion battery supply chain and energy transition materials. The company provides mine-to-grid supply chain data, price assessments, forecasts, and databases covering lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite, batteries, electric vehicles, rare earths, and permanent magnets. Benchmark's proprietary price assessment methodologies are assured to Type 2 IOSCO standards. API access is available to subscribers for programmatic integration of price data, supply chain data, and market intelligence into business systems and analytics platforms.

providers.name: HungryPanda
providers.description: HungryPanda (熊猫外卖) is the largest Asian food delivery platform serving overseas Chinese communities, founded in Nottingham, UK in 2017 and headquartered in London. It operates a marketplace app, a rider delivery network, the Panda Fresh Asian grocery e-commerce platform and the VouchersPanda lifestyle-deals platform across more than 80 cities in ten countries (UK, France, Italy, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and Singapore). Its API surface is a regionally partitioned merchant/partner ordering platform used by POS and middleware integrators — Deliverect, Otter, Neopos, Hubster, Menusifu, Easy Cloud and Redcat — to inject HungryPanda orders into a restaurant point of sale, push order-status updates back, and sync menus. Integration credentials (App Key, Secret Key, ShopID) are issued by HungryPanda on a partner basis; there is no public developer portal, no published specification and no self-service sign-up.

providers.name: Numina
providers.description: Numina is a New York City-based urban street-intelligence company (founded 2014, backed by 500 Global and SOSV) whose privacy-first, edge-processing computer-vision sensors measure how people, bicycles, and vehicles move through the public right-of-way. Its "Know Your Streets" platform turns anonymous, aggregated activity into multimodal mobility data for urban planners, municipal departments of transportation, and facilities managers, and exposes that data through the Numina Graph GraphQL API and a developer sandbox. (This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio stub under the placeholder label "CTY"; its Website pointer and 500 Global backing identify it as Numina / numina.co.)

providers.name: 2ULaundry
providers.description: 2ULaundry is a laundry and dry cleaning pickup-and-delivery service headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina and backed by Techstars. Customers schedule pickups through a mobile app, leave color-coded bags at their door, and receive cleaned items back within one to two business days. Services include residential wash-and-fold, delicate garment care, dry cleaning, and household linens, plus commercial laundry solutions for Airbnbs, spas, gyms, salons, and healthcare facilities. The company operates its own processing facilities and a fleet-based delivery network across its Southeast US markets. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Techstars portfolio and enriched; 2ULaundry is a consumer service company and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Fueloyal
providers.description: Fueloyal is an automotive IoT and connected-vehicle platform company that builds proprietary IoT gateway hardware and software for fleet management, fuel management, predictive maintenance, dual dash cameras, EV services, and OEM connected-vehicle solutions. Its products help fleets and vehicle manufacturers monitor, connect, and service vehicles, with an OEM connected-platform and marketplace for delivering connected-vehicle services and mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Fueloyal was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: hampr
providers.description: hampr is an app-based, on-demand laundry pickup and delivery service founded by Laurel Hess and backed by Techstars. Members bag their dirty laundry, tap the hampr mobile app, and a local independent "washr" collects, professionally washes, dries, folds, and returns it to their door within 24 hours at flat-rate per-load pricing with free pickup and delivery. hampr operates across 16+ US states with 1,500+ washrs, 11,000+ members, and 300,000+ loads completed, and also runs hampr for business, a commercial laundry solution for salons, spas, gyms, and short-term rentals. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; hampr is a consumer/commercial mobile service and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Helpling
providers.description: Helpling is an online marketplace that connects households with vetted, insured independent cleaners for on-demand and recurring home-cleaning services. Founded in Berlin and operating across 200+ cities in Germany and other European markets, the platform lets customers compare cleaner profiles and ratings, book and reschedule appointments, and pay online, with liability insurance covering each booking. Helpling operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile app product (iOS and Android) plus separate provider and agency portals; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. It was surfaced through the point-nine venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Rinse
providers.description: Rinse is a laundry and dry cleaning delivery service that picks up customers' clothes from home, professionally cleans them, and returns them on a recurring or one-off schedule. It runs a wash & fold and dry cleaning model in which uniformed valets handle evening pickup and delivery (typically 7pm-10pm) across major U.S. metros including the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Washington D.C., Boston, Seattle, and Austin, plus Toronto. Rinse emphasizes convenience, garment care, sustainability, and employing its valets as W-2 employees with benefits. The company is backed by Partech and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Rinse publishes a consumer web and mobile product but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Ridecell
providers.description: Ridecell is an AI-powered asset intelligence and orchestration platform for automotive leasing, fleet, and finance companies. Its five intelligence modules (Client, Spend, Supplier, Asset, and Operational Intelligence) and the "Maya" AI agent monitor fleets, flag invoice overcharges, track garage/supplier performance, optimize vehicle remarketing and residual value, and resolve idle-vehicle inefficiencies. The platform processes 12M+ events daily across 500K+ assets, 100+ connected systems, and 14+ countries. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Ridecell does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; this profile captures its public information, security, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: BC Hydro
providers.description: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (BC Hydro) is a provincial Crown corporation whose sole shareholder is the Province of British Columbia, and which states that it generates and delivers electricity to "95% of the population of B.C." and serves "over five million people." It is the vertically integrated end of the value chain in a market with no retail competition: BC Hydro owns the generation fleet (predominantly large hydroelectric), owns and operates the provincial transmission and distribution system, and is the monopoly retailer that bills the customer — all under rate regulation by the B.C. Utilities Commission (BCUC), not under any consumer data right. That regulatory fact drives the entire API posture. Ontario Regulation 633/21 compels Ontario distributors to implement Green Button Download My Data and Connect My Data; British Columbia has no equivalent, and no Canadian federal energy data mandate exists. BC Hydro has nonetheless adopted Green Button voluntarily — but only the file half of it. BC Hydro's own MyHydro billing pages state that a customer can "Download a CSV or Green Button XML file with your metered electricity use," available through the previous day and up to three years back. There is no Connect My Data, no OAuth authorization surface, no third-party vendor onboarding, and no published resource base URI: a third party cannot obtain a customer's usage data through any documented API, only the account holder can, by logging in and downloading a file. On the market-data side the picture is just as closed. There is no developer.bchydro.com, api.bchydro.com, data.bchydro.com or docs.bchydro.com (all DNS failures), no /developers, /api or /data path, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition anywhere, and no open data portal. Wholesale transmission information is posted to an OATI-hosted OASIS node that only registered transmission customers may use, and the BCUC-ordered transaction-data postings are documents rather than feeds. The single deliberate open-data artifact is one 2013 mapping layer published to the provincial BC Data Catalogue under the org "bc-hydro-and-power-authority." The finding is a utility that is closed on both axes: consumer data exists in a real standard but only as a human-initiated download behind a customer login, and grid/market data is either registration-gated or absent.

providers.name: Clutter
providers.description: Clutter is a full-service, on-demand storage and moving company (clutter.com) that picks up, professionally packs and photo-catalogs customers' belongings, stores them in secure 24/7-monitored warehouses, and redelivers individual items on demand. Founded in 2013 and once a SoftBank-backed unicorn, Clutter merged with MakeSpace and was acquired by Iron Mountain in 2023; it now operates as "Clutter by Iron Mountain" serving major US metros and Toronto. This is a consumer-facing services company with a customer account portal and booking flow but no public developer program or API; the record is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Moviation, Inc.
providers.description: Moviation, Inc. is a Seoul-based advanced air mobility and premium travel company founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. It operates Vonaer, an AI-powered luxury mobility platform that orchestrates on-demand travel across private aviation (jets and helicopters), luxury ground transportation (limousines), super yachts, and curated experiences, with planned expansion into electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) urban air mobility (UAM). Moviation currently runs air-taxi service with conventional helicopters and has partnered with hybrid-eVTOL developer Plana to build out an advanced air mobility (AAM) ecosystem in South Korea. The company reaches customers through the consumer Vonaer app and a concierge membership program; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: SmartHop
providers.description: SmartHop is a fleet and trip management platform for small trucking companies, owner-operators, and independent dispatchers. It aggregates real-time loads from multiple freight sources into a single load board and provides load booking, trip creation and management, dispatch management, payroll, profit optimization, market analysis, and performance reporting. SmartHop consumes third-party freight APIs from partners including DAT Freight & Analytics, C.H. Robinson, Loadsmart, Redwood Logistics, Newtrul, and Parade, but does not publish a public developer API of its own; its api.smarthop.co host backs the SmartHop web and mobile apps rather than a documented external API.

providers.name: Roadsurfer
providers.description: Roadsurfer is a Munich-based camper van, motorhome, and RV travel company founded in 2016, operating a fleet of 10,000+ vehicles across 100+ pick-up/drop-off locations in 16 countries in Europe and North America. Beyond flexible RV rentals it offers RV subscriptions, RV sales, one-way "Rallies," and roadsurfer Spots, a network of 10,000+ hand-picked European campsites. Roadsurfer is a consumer-facing brand with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and published llms.txt for the API Evangelist network. Backed by HV Capital.

providers.name: Parcel Monitor
providers.description: Global parcel tracking REST API aggregating real-time tracking data from 1,000+ carriers worldwide, enabling e-commerce shipment visibility, delivery analytics, and webhook-driven notifications across 170+ countries.

providers.name: Tier
providers.description: Tier (now operating as Dott following the 2024 merger of TIER Mobility and Dott) is a European micromobility operator providing shared e-scooters and e-bikes across more than 400 cities in Europe and the Middle East. The company exposes a partner-facing Dott Partner API — an API-Key-gated data feed (including GBFS-style vehicle-availability data) governed by its published API Licence — alongside consumer rider apps for iOS and Android. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Amsterdam, Tier/Dott was backed by Northzone, Point Nine, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Uptake
providers.description: Uptake Technologies is a Chicago-based industrial AI and predictive-maintenance software company founded in 2014 by Eric Lefkofsky and Brad Keywell. Its SaaS platform ingests telematics, sensor, fluid-analysis and work-order data from heavy commercial fleets and industrial assets, then applies machine-learning failure models — backed by an Asset Strategy Library of roughly 800 equipment types and tens of thousands of failure modes acquired with Asset Performance Technologies in 2018 — to predict component failure before it happens. Products include Uptake Fleet and Radar (predictive maintenance alerts), Compass (work-order data cleansing), Fusion (operational-technology data to cloud) and Scout (rules-based alerting), delivered through the fleet.uptake.com web application, a Geotab Marketplace add-in, and a customer-provisioned REST API gateway at api.uptake.com. Bosch announced its acquisition of Uptake in March 2026.

providers.name: Progressive Insurance
providers.description: One of the largest auto insurance providers in the United States offering personal auto, motorcycle, boat, RV, home, renters, and commercial insurance. Progressive is known for its direct-to-consumer model (1-800-PROGRESSIVE and progressive.com), its independent-agent channel, the comparative rate quoting experience, and the Snapshot usage-based insurance program that prices premiums against telematics-captured driving behaviour from a plug-in OBD-II dongle or the Snapshot mobile app. Progressive also runs the ForAgents agent portal and a public Developer Portal at developer.progressive.com that hosts embedded-quoting APIs for partners — including the Embedded Direct auto quoting API, the Commercial Auto Quoting product, and the Certificate of Insurance API — alongside private B2B integrations with comparative-rater carriers, agency-management systems, and telematics providers.

providers.name: Root Insurance
providers.description: Root is a U.S. app-first auto insurer that prices policies primarily on real driving behavior captured by smartphone telematics. The Root mobile app handles enrollment, telematics scoring, policy management, claims, and optional roadside assistance, with renters insurance as an add-on line. Root has reorganized its tech stack around APIs to power embedded auto insurance with partners such as Carvana and Hyundai Capital America; partner APIs are gated and not publicly documented. Note: Root Insurance (joinroot.com) is distinct from the unrelated Root Platform (rootplatform.com) insurtech in South Africa / UK.

providers.name: Bikemap
providers.description: Bikemap is a Vienna-based cycling platform (backed by Speedinvest) offering a route planner, turn-by-turn bike navigation, and one of the world's largest communities of user-generated cycling routes across road, mountain, gravel, and e-bike riding. Riders plan routes in a web and mobile route editor, discover millions of community routes, record and share rides, download offline maps, and sync with Garmin, Wahoo, Apple Watch, and Wear OS devices. Bikemap operates a consumer product surface (web, iOS, Android) and does not publish a documented public developer API; this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Drivio
providers.description: Drivio (Drivio Technologies Pvt Ltd) is a tech-enabled, omni-channel two-wheeler financing marketplace in India that connects motorcycle, scooter, and electric-vehicle buyers with banks and NBFCs. Founded in 2022 by Saurabh Tripathi and Ankur Bhardwaj and headquartered in the Delhi NCR region (Gurugram / New Delhi), the platform offers EMI calculators, instant eligibility checks, curated finance offers, vehicle comparison, and same-day loan approval and disbursal through lending partners including IDFC First Bank, Bajaj Auto Credit, L&T Financial Services, HDB Financial Services, Moneyplus Financial Services, and Arthmate. Drivio is an ISO/IEC 27001 certified company and is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Monarch Tractor
providers.description: Monarch Tractor is a Livermore, California agricultural-technology company that builds the MK-V, a fully electric, driver-optional smart tractor, together with WingspanAI (Wingspan Ag Intelligence) — an AWS-hosted farm-management and fleet-telemetry platform that collects in-field video, machine telemetry, energy and emissions data from connected tractors and presents it to growers through web and mobile apps. The company markets an "open ecosystem" in which third parties integrate with the MK-V and WingspanAI, and has pivoted toward selling autonomy as software and licensing its autonomy stack to other equipment makers. Monarch publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the WingspanAI platform is reachable only through a customer login.

providers.name: AtoB
providers.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: CloudTrucks
providers.description: CloudTrucks (operated by Cloud Technologies, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based virtual trucking carrier and business-management platform for owner-operators and small trucking fleets. The platform aggregates freight loads from more than fifty brokers and shippers into a single app, and layers on load booking, dispatching, real-time tracking, instant pay on proof of delivery, invoicing, factoring, fuel discounts (FuelApp), insurance, and back-office financial tooling so independent drivers can run their business from a phone. CloudTrucks also operates Exchange for shippers and brokers plus a freight-agent program, and is backed by Craft Ventures, Kindred Ventures and Menlo Ventures. CloudTrucks does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile captures its public web, legal, support and mobile-app surface plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Dance
providers.description: Dance is a Berlin-based electric mobility subscription company that offers e-bikes and e-mopeds as an all-in-one monthly subscription. A single fixed monthly fee bundles the vehicle together with on-demand repairs and maintenance, fast replacements, and theft protection, so members can ride without owning or servicing the hardware themselves. Dance operates in Berlin, Hamburg, and Paris, with product lines including the Dance One and Dance One Step e-bikes and the Dance Moped. Founded in 2020 by SoundCloud co-founders Alexander Ljung and Eric Quidenus-Wahlforss with Jimdo co-founder Christian Springub, Dance is a consumer-facing, app-based service backed by HV Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, help, and security surface.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: Spiffy
providers.description: Get Spiffy, Inc. (Spiffy) is a B2B SaaS and operations company that sells a mobile service operating system to franchise car dealerships. Its core product, Mobile 360, is an enterprise platform covering scheduling, dispatch, route optimization, technician management, digital vehicle inspections, DMS integration and customer communication, sold as a turnkey program alongside van upfits, connected devices (Easy Tread, Easy Flow, Smart Tumbler) and technician training. Spiffy also runs fleet and Amazon DSP service programs, and operates a customer booking portal and a fleet portal. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Apex, North Carolina, the company has raised more than $90M and reports over 4 million completed services, with OEM work including a Hyundai Motor America pilot. Spiffy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; its Fleet portal API is an internal, credentialed surface with no published contract.

providers.name: Avatr Technology
providers.description: AVATR Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. (阿维塔科技) is a Chinese premium intelligent electric-vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Chongqing, founded in 2018 as a joint venture in which Changan Automobile and CATL are the two largest shareholders and Huawei supplies the smart-cockpit and advanced driver-assistance stack. Its vehicles — the AVATR 11 and 12, the volume 06 and 07 (battery-electric and range-extended), and the limited 011 and 012 — are built on the jointly developed CHN smart-EV platform, a six-layer architecture spanning the mechanical, energy, electronic/electrical architecture, vehicle operating system, vehicle function application and cloud big-data layers. AVATR produced 73,606 vehicles in 2024 and sells through mainland China plus overseas markets including Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Qatar, with design and engineering offices in Shanghai and Munich. AVATR is a vehicle manufacturer, not a software vendor: www.avatr.com is a marketing and configurator site with no developer portal, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification. The only live agent surface anywhere on an AVATR hostname is platform-provided — the official Hong Kong site runs on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint plus a Wix-generated llms.txt over its public marketing content.

providers.name: VanMoof
providers.description: VanMoof is an Amsterdam-based e-bike company that designs and sells smart electric city bikes with integrated anti-theft technology, GPS tracking, and a companion rider app. Originally backed by Balderton Capital and relaunched after its 2023 restructuring, VanMoof operates a connected-bike platform, but publishes no public developer API — the app and bike APIs are private, and existing client libraries are community-built and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Wecasa
providers.description: Wecasa is a French on-demand home-services marketplace that connects households with vetted independent professionals who deliver the service at the customer's home. Its catalogue spans household cleaning and ironing, childcare and babysitting, mobile hairdressing, at-home beauty and nail care, massage and wellness, and personal fitness coaching. Customers book, schedule and pay through the Wecasa web site or the iOS/Android app; the professionals who fulfil the work run their business through the separate Wecasa Pro app. Founded in France and backed by Serena, the company operates in France, the United Kingdom, Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Wecasa publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract — the platform is a consumer application and a partner-onboarding funnel, not a developer product.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Mottu
providers.description: Mottu is the leading motorcycle-rental ecosystem in Latin America, founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, Brazil by Rubens Zanelatto. It rents motorcycles to gig and delivery couriers who lack access to traditional credit, bundling insurance, maintenance, 24-hour support and financial services (Mottu Pay) so workers can earn income through food delivery, e-commerce and last-mile logistics. Mottu has verticalized the value chain, running its own assembly line, parts and service network, and fleet-management software, and offers white-labeled last-mile delivery (Mottu Entregas) to more than 1,000 retailers across 100+ cities in Brazil and Mexico. Backed by QED Investors, Mottu has raised over US$150M. It operates as a consumer and B2B mobility/fintech app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Metropolis Technologies
providers.description: Metropolis Technologies is an AI-powered recognition platform that uses computer vision to make real-world physical spaces responsive, best known as the largest U.S. parking operator with checkout-free parking across 4,200+ North American locations. Founded in 2017, the company powers what it calls the "Recognition Economy" — vehicles are recognized on entry and exit so members pay automatically without tickets, gates, or lines. Metropolis scaled through the acquisitions of Premier Parking (2022) and SP Plus Corporation (2024), raised $1.6 billion in financing in 2025, and was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company of 2026. It is backed by Dragoneer. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public identity and security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Ambi Robotics
providers.description: Ambi Robotics is a Berkeley, California AI robotics company building parcel-sortation and induction robots for ecommerce, postal, and logistics workflows. Founded in 2018 as Ambidextrous Laboratories — a spin-out of UC Berkeley's Dex-Net Project led by Ken Goldberg — by Jeff Mahler (CTO), Stephen McKinley, David Gealy, and Matt Matl, with Jim Liefer (ex-Walmart, ex-UPS) as CEO. Its flagship products are AmbiSort A-Series (sort-to-sack small parcel sorting), AmbiSort B-Series (sort-to-gaylord parcel induction for middle-mile and reverse logistics), AmbiStack (mixed-case stacking for inbound and outbound), and AmbiVision (3D dimensioning, OCR, defect detection, and visual quality inspection). All robots run AmbiOS, the company's cloud-native "operating system for physical intelligence," comprising the AI Skill Suite (Sort, Stack, Kit, Pack, Induct apps), the PRIME-1 foundation model trained on millions of real-world operations, AmbiVision perception, AmbiAccess fleet management dashboard with heat maps and remote support, and a Sim2Real training pipeline that compresses model training by up to 10,000x. Ambi Robotics' primary commercial deployment is a $23 million expansion with Pitney Bowes, with AmbiSort A-Series and B-Series systems deployed across Pitney Bowes ecommerce hubs in the US (including the Stockton, CA hub that nearly doubled local-direct-delivery throughput in the 2021 peak holiday season, and middle-mile B-Series systems that sorted more than 3 million parcels within four months of deployment). Ambi Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for AmbiOS, AmbiSort, AmbiStack, or PRIME-1; integration with customer WMS/WES systems is performed by Ambi's solutions team. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (Ray, trimesh, FCL, EIPScanner, tinygltf, rapier, jszmq, CVXPYgen, mongoose-delete) and internal CI/CD workflow utilities — no published API spec, SDK package, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Hyundai
providers.description: Hyundai Motor Company is a South Korean multinational automotive manufacturer specializing in designing and producing a wide range of vehicles including cars, SUVs, and commercial vehicles. Hyundai operates a developer portal exposing connected vehicle services, mobility solutions, and partner integration touchpoints.

providers.name: LawnGuru
providers.description: LawnGuru is a lawn and landscape services marketplace that connects homeowners with vetted local service providers through a mobile-first platform. It offers instant pricing via aerial property mapping, real-time job tracking, and a satisfaction guarantee, spanning 17+ outdoor services including lawn mowing, snow clearing, yard cleanup, weeding, hedge trimming, gutter cleaning, tree work, seeding, aeration, mulch installation, pressure washing, sprinkler services, and junk removal. The company reports over 1,000,000 completed jobs. As of this enrichment pass, LawnGuru publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Slate Auto
providers.description: Slate Auto is an American electric-vehicle manufacturer building a radically simple, affordable, and customizable electric pickup truck. Designed in California and Michigan, engineered in Michigan, and assembled in the Midwest, the "Blank Slate" starts around $24,950 and offers roughly 205 miles of range, with interchangeable body panels and 200+ accessories that let owners reconfigure the vehicle over its life (including SUV and Fastback body styles). Slate sells direct through a preorder/reservation model, rejects mandatory feature packages and large touchscreens in favor of durability and owner control, and offers fleet solutions. Backed by General Catalyst. As a consumer automaker, Slate Auto publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Upciti
providers.description: Upciti is a French smart-city company that equips cities with intelligent computer-vision sensors and the Upciti OS platform, turning streets into clear, anonymous data for informed municipal decisions across parking, mobility, energy, water, gas, lighting, temperature, weather, air quality, pollen, illegal dumping, and noise. Sensors process video 100% locally with no image storage (GDPR-native, DTPR-supporting), and the platform advertises an open API for connecting GIS, BI, and business tools with no proprietary lock-in. Product documentation is customer-gated.

providers.name: Velocia
providers.description: Velocia is a transit ridership solutions company that uses real-time rewards, incentives, and digital tools to increase public-transit ridership and engagement for transit agencies and cities. Its programs include a Rider Incentive Program, Transit Ambassador Program, Mobility Wallet, rider surveys, an Automated Guaranteed Ride Home Program, and Major Event Solutions, integrated into transit apps to drive behavior change. Velocia partners with agencies and mobility services such as Miami-Dade County, King County Metro, Seattle DOT, Lime, Zipcar, Uber, Lyft, and CitiBike Miami. Founded in 2018 and based in Toronto, Velocia is a Techstars-backed company. This profile has no public developer/API surface at enrichment time.

providers.name: Fuse
providers.description: Fuse Energy is a UK retail energy supplier providing gas and electricity to homes and businesses, alongside EV charging, solar and battery storage tracking with grid export, and smart home energy management. The company emphasises savings against the UK price cap, a fast (~3 minute) online sign-up, automated supplier switching, and 24/7 customer support including an AI assistant called "Plugs". Fuse was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer/business energy web and mobile experience and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (Fuse Energy Supply Limited) is a UK-based residential and business energy supplier providing gas and electricity on variable, fixed, and multi-rate tariffs, alongside EV charging, solar and battery export tracking, multi-property account management, and an in-app AI energy assistant called Plugs. The company positions itself around beating the UK energy price cap, sign-up in under three minutes, and 24-hour customer support. It operates a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile app experience and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Ara
providers.description: Ara (Ara Labs, Inc.) is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising network that finances, installs, and operates rich-media displays across mobility, municipal, parking, and retail settings. It describes itself as the largest U.S. owner-operator of rideshare and taxi car-top digital billboards, running a long-term partnership with Uber alongside in-car, storefront, and parking/municipal kiosk screens. Ara owns the hardware and content-management operations under a monthly subscription model so fleet owners, retailers, parking operators and municipalities avoid cap-ex and operational overhead, and it also sells self-serve NYC taxi-top ad time by the hour or day. Its own site names Founders Fund, Coatue, Rosecliff Ventures, iHeart Media and Kellogg's as investors. Ara publishes NO public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation site or machine-readable specification. Contract discovery in August 2026 found a live private backend at api.arascreens.com (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) that answers every route with an HTTP Basic challenge, a React driver/operations application at app.arascreens.com, and a third-party signage CMS front end at cms.arascreens.com — all credentialed product infrastructure, none of it a developer offering. A second pass enumerated the full host inventory and added four more production hosts to the same finding: outdoor.arascreens.com (an SPA product page for the Ara O49 display), rts.arascreens.com (an unauthenticated Express service serving only its scaffold string), stationary.arascreens.com and assets.arascreens.com. Ara's marketing describes its CMS as "API-driven", meaning its own platform is programmatically operated and can integrate with a partner's existing signage stack — it is not an offer of a public API, and no key issuance, reference or access request mechanism exists anywhere on its surface.

providers.name: Freshop
providers.description: Freshop is an eCommerce platform purpose-built for grocery and specialty retail, now part of NCR Voyix. It powers branded online storefronts, mobile shopping, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery for independent and regional grocers, and integrates third-party services for loyalty, coupons, email, SMS, and fulfillment. Freshop exposes a live REST API at api.freshop.com that serves store and product data to Freshop-powered storefronts and apps, authenticated with an application key (app_key) query-string parameter and versioned by a numeric path segment.

providers.name: Grabr
providers.description: Grabr is a peer-to-peer cross-border shopping marketplace, founded in 2015 in San Francisco, that connects shoppers wanting products unavailable or expensive in their home country with travelers who deliver those items during trips in exchange for a reward. Grabr handles secure online payments, calculates duties and fees upfront, and holds funds in escrow until delivery is confirmed, operating across 75+ countries. It is a consumer mobile-app marketplace (iOS and Android) with a sibling fintech product, GrabrFi (US banking for non-residents). Grabr does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity, support, legal, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nirvana Tech
providers.description: Nirvana Insurance (Nirvana Tech, Inc.) is a technology-driven commercial trucking insurance provider that pairs A-rated fleet insurance coverage with an AI-powered active safety platform. Nirvana ingests telematics and connected-vehicle data from motor carriers to price risk more accurately, help fleets save up to 20% on premiums, and reduce accidents through real-time safety alerts, driver coaching, and predictive risk scoring. The company serves fleets and independent insurance agents through a digital quoting and policy-management agent portal, and is backed by General Catalyst. Nirvana raised a Series D round to expand its data-driven insurance and safety products across the trucking industry. As of this profile Nirvana operates a marketing site plus an agent sign-in portal and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Parkopedia
providers.description: With the roll-out of connected cars, services such as live traffic and live parking have become standard requirements. Parkopedia leads the market in parking data services, with 90 million parking spaces globally across 90 countries, available via the Parkopedia parking API or feed.

providers.name: Presto
providers.description: Presto Charging (Presto) is an electric-vehicle charging platform that aggregates access to 180,000+ public chargers across 20+ North American networks — including EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, BP Pulse, and Flo — behind a single mobile app, payment method, and account. For drivers it offers price comparison, real-time charger availability, and a unified charging experience on iOS and Android. For fleets and enterprises it delivers charge management, granular usage data, and white-label products so operators can "manage charging like they manage fuel." For charging networks it drives utilization and station profitability. Presto exposes OCPI-compliant, mobile-first APIs and SDKs so fleet-solution and mobility partners can embed public charging — including Plug and Charge and Autocharge — under their own brand. Backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Automotus
providers.description: Automotus is a smart-city and urban-mobility technology company that provides automated curb management using computer vision. Its CurbSight AI cameras use automatic license plate recognition (ALPR), 5G connectivity, edge processing, and privacy-by-design to monitor curb activity, while CurbPass handles curb access payment and invoicing and CurbSuite delivers an enforcement and analytics dashboard. Automotus works with cities, airports, and commercial fleets to reduce congestion, improve safety and compliance, cut emissions, and generate new curb revenue. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer/API surface has been found yet.

providers.name: BizzyCar
providers.description: BizzyCar is a B2B SaaS platform for automotive dealerships that automates service recall management, customer outreach and mobile service. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Saint Peters, Missouri, the company ingests VIN-level open-recall data from OEM partners, matches it against a dealer's market area and DMS records, then uses AI-driven outreach (SMS, email, voice) to book service appointments and dispatch mobile service vans. Products include Recall Outreach, Recall Scout, Recall Radar, Service Engine, Mobile Service and Fleet IQ. BizzyCar is primarily an API *consumer* rather than an API producer: it ships pre-built connectors into dealer management systems (Dealertrack, DMS Plus, Open/Mate, Asbury, PBS, Tekion, Fortellis, Reynolds & Reynolds) and service schedulers (Xtime, TCC, DealerFX, Affinitiv, Update Promise), but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract of its own.

providers.name: Blue White Robotics
providers.description: Blue White Robotics Ltd. — operating as Bluewhite — is an Israeli off-road autonomy company founded in 2017 by Ben Alfi, Yair Shahar and Aviram Shmueli, headquartered in Tel Aviv with a US operation in Fresno, California. Bluewhite builds an OEM-agnostic autonomy stack that retrofits conventional vehicles into unmanned ground vehicles: Pathfinder, an aftermarket autonomy kit combining control, intelligence and perception modules over a distributed CAN network, and Compass, a cloud fleet-operations SaaS that lets operators remotely supervise, task and monitor an autonomous fleet. The company began in permanent-crop agriculture — autonomous spraying, mowing and harvest support across roughly 150,000 US acres for 20-plus growers — and has since extended the same GPS-denied navigation and perception stack to defense and homeland-security ground robotics. Elbit Systems' FUSE acquired 100% of Blue White Robotics in 2026. Bluewhite markets a Software SDK and an "API platform" for OEM and system integration, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the Compass operator platform sits behind a Keycloak/OIDC login and integration access runs through a contact-sales form.

providers.name: Bonnet
providers.description: Bonnet is a UK-based electric vehicle (EV) charging app that aggregates multiple charging networks into a single platform, letting drivers find, access, and pay for chargers across Europe through one membership. Headquartered in Bristol and acquired by OVO Energy, it gives consumers real-time charger status, route planning, membership plans with per-charge savings, and weekly charging-credit rewards, while offering charge point operator (CPO) and fleet solutions with white-label integration for businesses. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Bonnet publishes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Evie Networks
providers.description: Evie Networks is an Australian electric-vehicle charging infrastructure company, founded in 2017 and backed by the St Baker Energy Innovation Fund, that owns and operates one of the country's largest DC fast and ultrafast public charging networks across 300+ locations in every state and territory. It sits downstream of the electricity retail market as a charge point operator (CPO) and e-mobility service provider, buying energy and reselling it as charging sessions to drivers and fleets, and it also builds and operates charging assets for site hosts, councils, dealerships and commercial property owners. Its API posture is closed: as of 2026-07-27 there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no named support for the EV charging interoperability standards (OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118). Evie is not a designated data holder under Australia's Consumer Data Right energy regime — the CDR Register's public energy data-holder brand summary lists 84 brands and Evie is not among them — so the statutory data mandate that produced identical APIs across Australian banks and energy retailers does not reach the EV charging layer at all. A live production API host exists at api.goevie.com.au serving the Evie Charging mobile app, but it is undocumented, unadvertised and returns a Google Cloud Endpoints 404 to anonymous callers. Neither consumer charging-session data nor network/market data is published through any documented public interface; charger location data reaches developers only through third-party aggregators.

providers.name: Freterium
providers.description: Freterium is a cloud-native AI Transport Management System (TMS) and unified logistics operating system that connects shippers, carriers, and fleets on a single intelligent layer. It spans first-mile, middle-mile, and last-mile operations across eight integrated modules — order management, AI-powered route planning, collaborative shipper and carrier portals, real-time GPS tracking with predictive ETAs, fleet management, freight billing and costing, intelligent document control, and analytics and reporting — and exposes a documented REST API for ERP/WMS integration alongside 50+ off-the-shelf telematics and hardware integrations. Surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Invygo
providers.description: Invygo is a car subscription and flexible rental platform founded in 2018 in Dubai, offering an alternative to traditional car ownership across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers subscribe to a car on a weekly or monthly basis, or enroll in a 36-month, Sharia-compliant "Subscribe to Own" plan, with insurance, maintenance, registration, and roadside assistance bundled into an all-inclusive fee and no deposit, salary certificate, or bank loan required. Invygo reports 20,000+ active subscriptions across 15+ cities in the GCC. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its public web, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: Leta
providers.description: Leta is a pan-African logistics technology company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya, with operations across Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. Leta builds an AI-driven delivery management platform that helps businesses move goods cheaper and faster while minimising climate impact: route optimization, automated dispatch and broadcast, live GPS track-and-trace, payment on delivery, fleet management, and delivery analytics. The platform is delivered as logistics SaaS plus on-demand and dedicated rider services, including an M-PESA business mini-app, and serves e-commerce, third-party logistics and courier, food and beverage, retail and consumer goods, and pharmacy and healthcare delivery operators. Leta is backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: AutoTrac
providers.description: AutoTrac is a Brazilian fleet management and vehicle tracking technology company with over 30 years of experience. As the national market leader, AutoTrac provides satellite and cellular fleet tracking solutions, real-time telemetry, driver journey management, and management intelligence platforms for logistics, agriculture, maritime, and insurance sectors. The company operates its own terrestrial satellite communication station and data center for nationwide coverage.

providers.name: Cowboy
providers.description: Cowboy is a Brussels-based mobility company that designs and manufactures premium connected electric bicycles for urban commuting. Its lineup — the Cruiser, Cruiser ST, Cross, and Cross ST — pairs a lightweight frame with removable batteries, integrated GPS tracking, crash detection, and its proprietary AdaptivePower motor assistance, all managed through the Cowboy mobile app. The company sells direct-to-consumer and through a network of 125+ service centers and mobile technicians across 40+ European cities, complemented by leasing, business, and student programs. Backed by Index Ventures, Cowboy operates a Shopify-based storefront and a connected-bike app platform; it does not publish a public developer API. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the company's real identity, legal, support, and security surfaces.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Jack in the Box
providers.description: Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK), founded in 1951 and headquartered in San Diego, California, is a quick-service restaurant company operating and franchising approximately 2,200 Jack in the Box hamburger restaurants across 21 U.S. states. In December 2021 the company acquired Del Taco for $575M; in August 2025 it announced a strategic review of Del Taco and on October 2025 agreed to divest Del Taco (~600 locations) to Yadav Enterprises for $115M, with the transaction closing December 22, 2025. Digital channels include the Jack in the Box mobile app, Jack Pack loyalty program, online ordering, and integrations with third-party delivery platforms (DoorDash, Grubhub, Uber Eats). The company does not publish a public developer API; all digital ordering, loyalty, and franchise systems are operated via internal platforms and partner integrations.

providers.name: Acme Markets
providers.description: Acme Markets is a regional supermarket chain founded in 1891 and headquartered in the U.S. Northeast, operating approximately 164 stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, New York, Connecticut, and Maryland. Acme is a banner of Albertsons Companies, Inc., one of the largest food and drug retailers in the United States. The brand has no publicly documented developer program or public API: digital surfaces (store locator, loyalty program "ACME for U", FreshPass subscription, DriveUp & Go, delivery, pharmacy) are delivered through Albertsons-shared web and mobile platforms. The Android package ID (`com.safeway.client.android.acme`) confirms that the Acme app is built on the shared Safeway/Albertsons banner application, suggesting a shared backend API surface across Albertsons banners that is not externally published.

providers.name: Buncha
providers.description: Buncha is a scheduled neighborhood grocery delivery service operating across Minnesota and Michigan. Customers shop online from local partner retailers and receive their orders on set weekly routes, with a single refrigerated van consolidating multiple neighbors' orders into one trip for a $3.45 flat delivery fee. Professional personal shoppers hand-pick items into insulated bags, and the aggregated-route model is positioned to cut delivery CO2 emissions by up to 80% versus on-demand services. Buncha is offered through iOS and Android consumer apps and is backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. It is currently a consumer product with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Zeel
providers.description: Zeel is an on-demand wellness marketplace that connects consumers with licensed, background-checked massage therapists for in-home, in-hotel, in-office, and event chair massage delivered same-day and often within an hour of booking. The platform covers a range of modalities including Swedish, deep tissue, sports, prenatal, sleep, and couples massage, and offers memberships, gift certificates, and a spa-staffing service (Zeel Spa Staffing) that supplies therapists to hotels and spas. Zeel operates a consumer-facing web and mobile booking experience across dozens of US metros; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or partner integration program.

providers.name: Astera Labs
providers.description: Astera Labs, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALAB) is a semiconductor company building purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI and cloud infrastructure. Its Intelligent Connectivity Platform spans the Aries PCIe/CXL Smart DSP Retimers, Smart Cable Modules and Smart Gearboxes, the Taurus Ethernet Smart Retimers and Smart Redrivers, the Leo CXL Smart Memory Controllers, and the Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches, all managed by COSMOS (COnnectivity System Management and Optimization Software). COSMOS is the software layer of the platform: firmware modules on the devices plus platform-level libraries that run on hosts and baseboard management controllers, exposing what Astera Labs describes as a single standardized API for device discovery, configuration, security attestation, firmware update, telemetry, link diagnostics, RAS testing, scripting and fleet management.
