That API surface is an on-premises host/BMC SDK rather than a public web API: the COSMOS Developer Kit is offered through a "Contact Us" motion and the supporting application notes are released through a document-request form, so no public API reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Rimac Automobili
providers.description: Rimac Automobili d.o.o. is a Croatian electric hypercar manufacturer and automotive technology company founded by Mate Rimac in 2009 and headquartered at the Rimac Campus in Kerestinec, near Zagreb. It designs and builds the Nevera and Nevera R all-electric hypercars, and develops the vehicle software, infotainment, connectivity and telemetry stack that runs them in-house. Since the 2021 formation of the Bugatti Rimac joint venture with Porsche, the group's component and OEM-supply business was carved out into the sister company Rimac Technology, while Rimac Automobili remains the vehicle brand. Rimac operates a private, customer-only connected-vehicle backend — an MQTT-based telemetry platform feeding first-party iOS and Android owner apps with location, charging, battery and driving-performance data, plus over-the-air update and remote command channels — but it publishes no public developer program, developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Weee
providers.description: Weee! is America's largest online Asian grocery store and delivery platform, operating as a direct-to-consumer online supermarket serving major metropolitan areas across the United States. It curates and fulfills inventory through regional distribution centers and cold-chain logistics, bringing together products and ingredients commonly found in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and Indian supermarkets. The storefront spans fresh produce, frozen meats, seafood, pantry staples, snacks, sauces, hot pot ingredients, beverages, and household essentials, accepts EBT/SNAP in eligible cities, and runs a multilingual experience (English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai). Weee is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile Weee publishes no public developer API; this record captures its public web identity and AI-indexing (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: Zipcar
providers.description: Zipcar is a Boston, Massachusetts-based car sharing service operating in more than 500 cities across North America and Europe, including major US metros (Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia, Portland, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington DC) and Canadian cities (Toronto, Hamilton, the Golden Horseshoe). Members reserve vehicles by the hour or day through the Zipcar mobile app, unlock cars with their phone, and pay per usage with gas, EV charging, standard damage protection insurance, and professional maintenance included. Zipcar serves consumer members, universities (Zipcar for Universities), and businesses (Zipcar for Business) with weekday fleet programs. Zipcar is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Avis Budget Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAR), which acquired the company in March 2013 for approximately $500 million. Zipcar exposes a REST-based Partner API at api.zipcar.com/partner-api, documented at owa.zipcar.com/documentation, that returns JSON for Location List and Location Detail resources (vehicles available at a lat/long); access is gated and granted on request via developerportal@zipcar.com — there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or self-service developer signup. Zipcar also operates a public GitHub organization (github.com/Zipcar) hosting internal DevOps tooling (Concourse resources, Ansible helpers, BOSH helpers, monitoring agents) rather than client-facing API artifacts.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: Blink Charging
providers.description: Blink Charging Co. (Nasdaq BLNK) operates the Blink Network of Level 2 and DC Fast electric vehicle chargers across North America and Europe, alongside brands acquired via SemaConnect, Blue Corner, BlueLA, and Envoy. Blink's charger hardware (Series 7/8/9) is OCPP 2.0.1 certified for CSMS interoperability, and in 2025 Blink joined Hubject's Intercharge eRoaming platform as a charge point operator using the OCPI protocol so third-party e-mobility service providers can route drivers and billing to Blink stations. Blink also runs a gated BlinkMap API developer program (station locations, hours, and live network status) and a Blink Fleet platform that partners such as Presto and BetterFleet integrate with via API for fleet charging, sessions, and billing. None of these programs currently publish a full public self-serve API reference; access requires signing up directly with Blink.

providers.name: Finn
providers.description: FINN (finn.com) is a Munich-based consumer car-subscription service that lets individuals and businesses lease a car on a flexible monthly subscription, with insurance, maintenance, registration, taxes, and roadside assistance bundled into one all-inclusive price. Subscribers pick from more than twenty vehicle brands on terms from six to twenty-four months, and the company also runs a fleet/business offering. Backed by HV Capital, FINN operates in Germany, the United States, and other European markets. FINN is a consumer, direct-to-customer business with no public developer API or partner API program surfaced at this time; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hitachi Construction Machinery
providers.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery provides operational data about machines and equipment on construction sites through the Telematics API, which complies with the ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) standard. The API enables higher efficiency, productivity, and safety while reducing life cycle costs.

providers.name: Flease
providers.description: Flease is a French vehicle-leasing marketplace offering flexible long-term (LLD, 24-50 month) and medium-term (LMD, 1-12 month) car and utility-vehicle rental to SMEs and small businesses. It sources quasi-new vehicles (under two years old, fewer than 30,000 km), delivers within a week for LMD and a month for LLD, and bundles a fleet-management web application (webapp.flease.fr) for tracking mileage, drivers, maintenance, contracts, and invoices. Flease positions on transparent pricing and a roughly 20% lower total cost of ownership versus traditional leasing, with a circular-economy angle of redeploying used vehicles. Backed by Partech. No public developer API or documentation is published; the customer-facing webapp is a Vue single-page app authenticated with AWS Cognito.

providers.name: ParkPow
providers.description: ParkPow is software to manage and enforce parking lots. It lets you track vehicles, get custom alerts, and enforce your parking rules. The ParkPow API documentation requires application access and is not publicly available.

providers.name: Tiff's Treats
providers.description: Tiff's Treats is an Austin, Texas cookie company founded in 1999 by University of Texas students Tiffany Taylor and Leon Chen, built around warm, baked-to-order cookies delivered same-day. The company operates roughly 90 bakery-storefronts across Texas and the southern and western United States, combining walk-in retail with an owned delivery fleet, an online ordering platform at cookiedelivery.com, and iOS and Android ordering apps. Alongside consumer delivery it runs a substantial corporate gifting, catering, e-gift-card and special-events business, plus an "Elites" subscription membership and a rewards program. Tiff's Treats has raised more than $50 million in outside investment, including a $25 million round led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, and counts Andy Roddick, Brooklyn Decker, Kendra Scott and Dirk Nowitzki among its investors. It is a direct-to-consumer food and delivery operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Lawn Love
providers.description: Lawn Love is an on-demand lawn care and outdoor home services marketplace that matches homeowners with vetted, independent lawn care professionals across more than 120 US cities. Customers get instant online quotes and book mowing, fertilization, aeration, seeding, pre-emergent and general weed control, bush trimming, leaf removal, gutter cleaning, yard clean-up and snow removal, on either pay-as-you-go or recurring schedules, and manage jobs through the my.lawnlove.com customer app and iOS/Android apps; providers take and service work through pros.lawnlove.com and the Lawn Love for Providers apps. Lawn Love operates as part of LawnStarter. It publishes no public developer API, no developer portal and no API documentation - the api.lawnlove.com host is an undocumented, noindexed backend serving its own web and mobile clients.

providers.name: Coco Robotics
providers.description: Coco Robotics is a Santa Monica, California urban robotics company operating a fleet of zero-emission, remotely-supervised sidewalk delivery robots ("Cocobots") for last-mile food, grocery and retail delivery. Merchants do not integrate with Coco directly: Coco is consumed as a delivery service provider through Uber Eats, DoorDash, Wolt and Olo Dispatch, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or webhooks of its own. Its public software surface is limited to a marketing site, a customer order-tracking web app, and a GitHub organization of forked ROS and infrastructure tooling.

providers.name: Datakrew
providers.description: Datakrew is a Singapore-based deep-tech company, a spin-off from NTU Singapore supported by Enterprise Singapore, building EV battery intelligence, fleet management, and AI-driven telematics for logistics and delivery, public transport, vehicle OEMs, rental/leasing and shared mobility operators, and mining and construction fleets. Its integrated hardware, software, and AI stack spans the OxRed (MyFleet) fleet-management and intelligence platform, OxRed Lens camera-based visualization telematics, OxRed AutoCert automated certification and compliance, GuardianAI driver-safety and collision-warning analytics, the Ask OX natural-language fleet assistant, and the ITUS Max and ITUS AutoScan edge terminals for telemetry, CAN-bus integration, and vehicle diagnostics, all aimed at optimizing battery health, safety, and operational efficiency.

providers.name: VCNC
providers.description: VCNC is a South Korean mobile technology company behind Between, a private messaging and photo-sharing app for couples, and TADA, a ride-hailing and mobility service operating in Korea. A 500 Global portfolio company, VCNC maintains an open source presence on GitHub, including Haeinsa, a multi-row transaction library for HBase published on Maven Central. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API client SDKs.

providers.name: Gridwiz
providers.description: Gridwiz Inc. is a South Korean clean-energy software and hardware company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seoul. It operates one of Korea's largest demand response (DR) aggregation portfolios, gathering electricity that industrial and commercial customers curtail and selling it into the national power market, and it pairs that with energy storage (ESS), renewable energy / RE100 and PPA advisory, and an e-mobility line covering EV charging controllers, CCS communication modems (EVCC/SECC), bidirectional V2G chargers and the Skyblue consumer charging service. Its e-mobility products are built to the international EV charging standards DIN SPEC 70121, ISO 15118 (including 15118-20 AC/DC) and OCPP, and its demand response management system is described as OpenADR-based. Gridwiz sells energy services and certified hardware to utilities, EVSE suppliers and enterprises; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Parklio
providers.description: Seamlessly integrate your existing systems or products with Parklio API so you can scale your operations and monitor parking space usage in real time. It provides access to your data in a way that works best for you, whether through integration, automation, or full customization. The API is RESTful with JSON responses, and Android and iOS SDKs are available on request.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: Transfercar
providers.description: Transfercar is a free vehicle relocation marketplace that connects rental car and motorhome companies who need vehicles moved between their depots with travelers willing to drive those vehicles one-way. Rental operators list relocation deals for cars and campervans that need to be repositioned, and drivers book them to travel between cities at little or no rental cost, often with extras such as free days, fuel allowances, or ferry contributions. The service operates across New Zealand, Australia, and the United States as a consumer-facing web booking platform rather than a developer API provider. Transfercar was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; this profile has been enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Asaak
providers.description: Asaak is an East African fintech company, headquartered in Kampala, Uganda, that provides asset financing and working capital to small businesses and individual entrepreneurs who are underserved by traditional banks. Its core products are loans for boda boda motorcycles, fuel, and smartphones, delivered through a mobile-first application with a simple four-step flow of apply, qualify, receive financing, and repay to build credit. Asaak operates branches across Uganda (Kampala, Jinja, Mukono, Matugga, Nabbingo, Fort Portal, Gulu, and Soroti) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It runs a backend admin platform at api.asaak.net and a Wix-hosted marketing site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access to public site content. Asaak does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: FreshToHome
providers.description: FreshToHome (Freshtohome Foods Private Limited) is a Bangalore-headquartered direct-to-consumer e-commerce company selling fresh, antibiotic-residue-free fish, seafood, poultry, mutton, ready-to-cook and heat-and-eat food. Founded in 2015 by Shan Kadavil, Mathew Joseph and Jayesh Jose, it runs its own farm-and-boat-to-doorstep cold chain, sourcing from thousands of fishermen and farmers and delivering across cities in India and the United Arab Emirates. The company sells through its website and its consumer iOS and Android apps. It publishes an llms.txt at its web root but operates no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Gridwise
providers.description: Gridwise is an earnings-tracking and optimization platform for rideshare and delivery gig workers, aggregating mileage, trip, and income data across gig platforms such as Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Grubhub, Instacart, and Amazon Flex so drivers can see where they earn most and drive more strategically. Alongside the consumer app, Gridwise operates Gridwise Analytics, a B2B mobility-data business that turns millions of anonymized driver location, trip, and earnings records into industry benchmarking, KPI, and market-intelligence products for gig mobility platforms, financial services, retailers/merchants, and autonomous vehicle fleets. Data is delivered as aggregated weekly reports, record-level trip datasets, and consumer/driver surveys through commercial engagement. Gridwise does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer, data-product, support, and policy surfaces.

providers.name: Vay
providers.description: Vay is a Berlin-headquartered teledriving (remote driving) mobility company, founded in 2018 by Thomas von der Ohe, Fabrizio Scelsi, and Bogdan Djukic, that operates the first commercial remotely driven car service. Customers in Las Vegas rent cars by the minute that are delivered and parked driverless by professional remote drivers from a Remote Driving Center; the company runs a 175-vehicle fleet, has served 50,000+ trips, and raised a Series C from Grab in December 2025. Vay is a consumer mobility service and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Atom Power
providers.description: Atom Power, Inc. is a Charlotte, North Carolina electrical technology company founded in 2014 that invented the Atom Switch, the world's first commercial UL-listed digital solid-state circuit breaker. The company builds SiC (silicon carbide) power modules, solid-state switchgear and panel-level Level 2 electric-vehicle charging hardware for commercial, industrial, data-center and grid-edge deployments, paired with cloud software for energy management, load balancing and charger operations. Atom Power previously ran an "Atom Cloud" developer portal on Azure API Management at developers.atompower.com with a gateway at api.atompower.com; both hostnames are now dangling CNAMEs to deleted Azure API Management instances, so no public API contract is currently reachable.

providers.name: Iontra
providers.description: Iontra Inc. is a Denver, Colorado battery technology company that develops proprietary Charge-Control technology for rechargeable lithium batteries. Founded in 2013 and publicly launched in 2022, Iontra applies electrodynamic sensing and signal processing during charging to suppress lithium plating, dendrite growth and SEI-layer expansion, claiming up to 4x cycle life, 2x faster charging, improved cold-weather charging and better safety without changing cell chemistry. The technology is chemistry agnostic across Li-ion, Li-metal, Li-S, solid-state and Na-ion cells, and is delivered to OEMs as custom charging algorithm "recipes" flashed onto an application-specific microcontroller, or as a software-only library. Iontra closed a $45M Series C led by Volta Energy Technologies to launch an integrated RISC-V charge-control and fuel-gauge MCU. Iontra is an embedded/silicon company: it publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI, and no public SDK packages — its SDK is firmware delivered to OEM customers through a login-gated Document Portal under commercial engagement.

providers.name: Meshcrafts
providers.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

providers.name: MoveYou
providers.description: Our scaled based platform meets all your business requirements in the fields of mobility and energy. Explore the powerful solutions or consult one of our experts for advice. Together, we are building a sustainable future for your organization.

providers.name: StoreDot
providers.description: StoreDot is an Israeli battery technology company founded in 2012 by Doron Myersdorf, Simon Litsyn and Gil Rosenman, headquartered in Herzliya with an advanced technology campus in Irvine, California. It develops extreme fast charging (XFC) lithium-ion cells built on proprietary silicon-dominant anode chemistry and synthesized organic and inorganic compounds optimized with machine-learning models, targeting the range and charging anxiety that gate mainstream electric-vehicle adoption. Its "100inX" product roadmap sets 100 miles of range charged in 5 minutes (100in5, 2024), 3 minutes (100in3, 2028) and 2 minutes (100in2, 2032); the company has demonstrated pouch and prismatic XFC cells sustaining more than 1,000 and later 2,000 extreme fast charging cycles while retaining over 80 percent of original capacity, and designs its chemistry to drop into existing Li-ion production lines. Strategic investors and partners include Daimler/Mercedes-Benz, BP, VinFast, Volvo, Polestar, Ola Electric, Samsung Ventures, TDK and manufacturing partner EVE Energy. In 2026 a planned SPAC merger with Andretti Acquisition Corp. II was terminated and the company returned to private fundraising. StoreDot is a hardware, materials and cell-manufacturing business: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server or machine-readable API contract, and no /.well-known/ discovery surface, llms.txt or developer subdomain resolves on store-dot.com.

providers.name: Jingle
providers.description: Jingle is a consumer marketplace mobile app for fast, direct local deliveries from mobile stores and services — "shops-on-wheels" — operating in the San Francisco Bay Area. Users sign up with a phone number (no password) and enable push notifications to be alerted when their favorite mobile vendors are nearby — artisanal food trucks, farmers'-market sellers, and one-click services such as bike repair, car wash, manicures, pedicures, and knife sharpening — then request a "jingle" to summon them. Deliveries are handled directly by the businesses themselves, cutting out delivery middlemen. Merchants use the app at their discretion to broadcast their presence to nearby neighborhoods, and residential complexes can partner to bring vendors on-site. Jingle is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its public consumer and merchant surface.

providers.name: Scape
providers.description: Scape (Scape Wellness) is an on-demand wellness technology platform in Latin America that lets customers book professional spa experiences delivered to their home, apartment, hotel, Airbnb, office, or corporate event. Certified, identity-verified therapists arrive with all required equipment — professional massage table, towels, oils, and materials. The catalog spans relaxing, deep tissue, sports, prenatal, lymphatic drainage, reflexology, and couples massages; facials; body treatments; and combined facial-plus-massage experiences, alongside personal and corporate gift cards and workplace wellness programs. Scape operates in Mexico, Colombia, Chile, and the Dominican Republic via iOS and Android apps, with payments through MercadoPago and PayPal. It is a consumer booking platform and does not publish a public developer API or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Whill
providers.description: WHILL, Inc. designs and manufactures enhanced personal mobility solutions — electric power chairs and mobility scooters, including the Model C2, Model F, the Modo Breeze ultralight foldable wheelchair, and the Model R three- and four-wheel scooters — and operates an autonomous personal mobility service that has completed over 700,000 rides worldwide across airports and other venues. WHILL was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this writing it is a consumer hardware and mobility-service company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record and will be enriched if WHILL launches a developer program.

providers.name: Zum
providers.description: Zum is a student transportation technology company that runs school bus operations for K-12 school districts through its Connected Mobility Experience (CMX) platform. Founded by Ritu Narayan and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Zum unifies parents, students, drivers, and district administrators with real-time ride tracking, route optimization, parent notification apps, driver tooling, fleet management dashboards, and an electrified bus program. The company serves roughly 6,500 schools and districts, has completed more than 159 million rides, and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. Zum operates consumer-facing parent and driver mobile apps and district dashboards, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Carwow
providers.description: Carwow is a UK-based online automotive marketplace that helps consumers buy, sell, lease, and finance cars without haggling or hidden fees. Buyers browse new and used car deals, compare dealer quotes, arrange leasing (including salary sacrifice and fleet through Carwow Leasey), find electric-vehicle deals, and access vehicle financing and credit brokering. Sellers get free car valuations, part-exchange, and van sales. Carwow also publishes professional car reviews and ratings, runs a large YouTube channel, and offers comparison tools, EV charging maps, a car history checker, and insurance services. Founded in London and backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Carwow operates across the UK and Europe. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source engineering tooling but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Ike Robotics (Nuro)
providers.description: Nuro is an autonomous-vehicle technology company that builds the Nuro Driver, an AI-first self-driving system it now licenses to automakers and mobility providers rather than operating its own delivery fleet. Nuro acquired the assets and team of Ike Robotics, an autonomous-trucking startup, folding that self-driving expertise into its Level 4 autonomy platform. The company partners with firms such as Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis and other autonomous applications, and pairs the Nuro Driver with the Nuro Toolkit for validation and deployment. Nuro operates a B2B licensing model and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Indrive
providers.description: inDrive is a global ride-hailing, delivery, and urban-services platform built around a peer-to-peer, name-your-price model in which passengers propose a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline it directly. Founded in 2012 by Arsen Tomsky in Yakutsk, Russia and now headquartered in Mountain View, California, the company operates across roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. Beyond city rides it offers intercity transport, courier and freight delivery, on-demand task services, and driver lending. inDrive was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and General Catalyst. inDrive does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; its GitHub organization hosts internal engineering frameworks and an engineering handbook rather than external API definitions.

providers.name: Sonatus
providers.description: Sonatus, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California automotive software company, founded in 2018, that builds cloud-to-edge vehicle AI software for software-defined vehicles (SDVs). Its Fastlane platform pairs in-vehicle Fastlane Edge software with Fastlane Collector for dynamic, policy-driven vehicle data collection, Fastlane Insight for cloud-side analysis, and Fastlane Copilot for quick-start integration, alongside the Sonatus Automator vehicle-automation product. Sonatus states its technology is deployed in more than eight million vehicles worldwide, and it is backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Kia, LG, Marvell, NEC, Foxconn and Translink Capital. Sonatus sells to vehicle OEMs and tier-one suppliers rather than to individual developers: it markets an SDK comprising Sonatus Automator, APIs and documentation, but that developer surface is delivered to contracted OEM customers and is not published on any public developer portal.

providers.name: Virtuo
providers.description: Virtuo (govirtuo.com) is a Paris-based, next-generation car rental company founded in 2015 and backed by Balderton Capital. It replaces the traditional rental counter with a mobile app: customers book, unlock, and return premium connected vehicles (Mercedes, BMW, Audi, Peugeot, Renault, Toyota, Volkswagen and others) entirely from their phone, with delivery options, free cancellation, and 24/7 support across 100+ locations in Europe. Virtuo also runs a "Virtuo for Business" corporate program and has committed to offsetting 100% of trips and electrifying its fleet by 2030. Virtuo does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Calvis
providers.description: Calvis is a multi-agency security guard marketplace that connects businesses with vetted, state-licensed, background-checked security guards from multiple professional agencies across 40+ US cities. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Miami, Florida, the platform pairs on-demand booking with AI-powered deployment matching, real-time GPS tracking and geofencing, live AI coaching delivered to guards through an earpiece, and automated incident reporting and site analytics. Businesses book unarmed, armed, event, retail, construction, corporate, residential, hospital, cannabis, and school security through the web platform and iOS/Android apps, while security professionals join the network to find work. Calvis is backed by Version One Ventures.

providers.name: Leapmotor
providers.description: Leapmotor (Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology Co., Ltd., HKEX: 9863) is a Chinese intelligent electric vehicle manufacturer founded in 2015 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China, which sold its first vehicles in 2019. Leapmotor designs and builds battery-electric and range-extended (REEV) passenger vehicles — including the T03 city car and the B03X, B05, B10 and C10 SUVs — on its own vertically integrated LEAP platform, developing its electric drive, battery, and intelligent cockpit and driving systems in house. Stellantis took a stake in the company in 2023 and, through the Leapmotor International joint venture, distributes Leapmotor vehicles across Europe and other export markets via leapmotor.net. Leapmotor operates connected-vehicle services — the Leapmotor mobile app, OTA software updates, and the Leapmotor Connected Experience — but publishes no public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation; the vehicle cloud interfaces used by its mobile app are private and only reached through unofficial, reverse-engineered community clients.

providers.name: Wingstop
providers.description: Wingstop Inc. (NASDAQ: WING) is a US-based quick-service restaurant chain specializing in cooked-to-order chicken wings, tenders, and sides across thousands of franchised and company-owned locations. Wingstop is digital-first - digital transactions account for the large majority of systemwide sales - built on its proprietary MyWingstop ordering platform and the Club Wingstop loyalty program, with consumer ordering via wingstop.com, native iOS and Android apps, and third-party delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub). Wingstop does not operate a public developer program or publish open API documentation. There is no developer.wingstop.com (the host does not resolve), and ordering, loyalty, menu, and POS integrations flow through bilateral corporate and franchisee technology programs rather than open developer endpoints.

providers.name: Zero Motorcycles
providers.description: Zero Motorcycles is an American manufacturer of electric motorcycles and powertrains, founded in 2006 in Santa Cruz, California. It designs and builds street, dual-sport and off-road electric motorcycles across its S, DS, FX and X lines — including the SR/S, SR/F, DSR/X, FXE and XE — around a proprietary Z-Force electric powertrain and aircraft-grade aluminum frame. Its bikes run the Cypher operating system, which pairs with the Zero Motorcycles NextGen mobile app over Bluetooth and cellular telematics for ride data, remote diagnostics, over-the-air updates and performance customization, and with the Cypher Store, where owners purchase software upgrades that unlock additional power, top speed and features. Zero sells internationally through a dealer network and serves retail, fleet and authority/first-responder segments. Its connected-vehicle platform is consumer-facing only: Zero publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: InDrive (fka inDriver)
providers.description: InDrive (formerly inDriver) is a global mobility and urban-services platform operating in roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. It is built on a distinctive peer-to-peer, user-proposed pricing model in which riders name a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline, rather than an algorithm setting the price. Beyond ride-hailing, InDrive spans intercity (city-to-city) rides, courier and freight delivery, and financial services, and is expanding into a "super app" for frontier markets. InDrive does not currently publish a public third-party developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public company, engineering, and legal surface.

providers.name: Advano
providers.description: Advano is a New Orleans, Louisiana battery-materials company that develops silicon-based anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Spun out of Tulane University in 2016 and backed by 25+ patents, its flagship REALSi silicon-carbon composite is engineered as a drop-in replacement for graphite anodes, delivering up to 9x the energy density of graphite for electric vehicles, consumer electronics, defense, and grid energy storage. Advano's process avoids hazardous silane gas, uses abundant metallurgical-grade silicon, and runs on existing manufacturing equipment. The company operates a pilot plant in New Orleans East and is scaling toward 3,000 tons of REALSi in 2026 and 20,000 tons by 2030. This is a physical deep-tech manufacturer with no public API or developer platform; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Battery Smart
providers.description: Battery Smart is India's largest battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, founded in 2019 by Pulkit Khurana and Siddharth Sikka and operated from New Delhi by Upgrid Solutions Private Limited and Upgrid Electrilease Private Limited. It runs an asset-light, partner-led model: local businesses — kirana stores, petrol pumps and neighbourhood shops — host swap points where a driver exchanges a depleted lithium-ion pack for a charged one in roughly two minutes and pays per swap instead of buying the battery with the vehicle, which removes the single largest cost from an electric two- or three-wheeler. The network is concentrated in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow, and the company has raised across eleven rounds including a USD 65 million Series B led by LeapFrog Investments with MUFG Bank, Panasonic, Ecosystem Integrity Fund, Blume Ventures and British International Investment participating, plus a USD 15 million debt round with Mirova in April 2026. Battery Smart's software ships only as end-user Android applications — Battery Smart Driver and Battery Smart Partner — backed by a production API host at api.upgrid.in that self-identifies as the "Battery Smart API". As of this profile the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Bolt.Earth
providers.description: Bolt.Earth operates what it describes as India's largest EV charging network, with more than 100,000 charging points deployed across 2,100+ cities. The company sells EV charging hardware (3.3kW smart sockets for 2/3/4-wheelers, AC chargers from 7.4kW to 22kW, and DC fast chargers from 30kW to 240kW) alongside a Charging Management System (CMS) for operators and a consumer mobile app for locating, booking, and paying for charging sessions. Services span site assessment, installation, KYC onboarding, charger activation, remote firmware updates, and 24/7 support for individuals, RWAs, enterprises, fleet operators, hospitality venues, highways, and government agencies. Bolt.Earth is backed by Version One Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an energy-sector company profile. No public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Cake
providers.description: Cake (stylized CAKE) is a Stockholm, Sweden based maker of premium, lightweight, high-performance electric motorcycles and mopeds, built around a mission to accelerate the shift to a zero-emission society by combining excitement with responsibility. Its clean-mobility lineup spans commuter models (Makka, Osa), off-road bikes (Kalk, Bukk) and work-focused utility variants. Founded by Stefan Ytterborn and backed by Creandum, CAKE filed for bankruptcy in early 2024 and its brand and IP were acquired by Norway's Brages Holding AS, which relaunched the company. Cake sells direct to consumers and through dealers at ridecake.com. Its bikes ship with the CAKE Connect module, and CAKE markets a "CAKE API" on its own :work and delivery pages that lets fleet owners pull vehicle data, telemetry and controls into their own fleet software — but that API has no public developer portal, no reference and no machine-readable specification; access runs through the contact and partner forms.

providers.name: Cycle
providers.description: CYCLE (operated by CM Invest B.V., Amsterdam) is a European electric-mobility subscription service that provides e-bikes and cargo bikes to professional delivery riders, couriers, and businesses. Its all-inclusive monthly subscriptions bundle maintenance, on-site repairs, bike swaps, GPS tracking, theft protection, and remote motor control across 100+ cities in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, Italy, and the UK. CYCLE was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the provider publishes a consumer/business marketing and operations site but exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Drover AI
providers.description: Drover AI is a Los Angeles-based micromobility technology company that pioneers the use of computer vision, machine learning, and proprietary sensor fusion in shared light electric vehicles (LEVs) such as e-scooters and e-bikes. Its flagship PathPilot module is a plug-and-play IoT unit retrofit onto existing fleet vehicles that delivers granular infrastructure distinction (sidewalk, bike lane, crosswalk, street), real-time parking validation, and the ability to control vehicle behavior (speed reduction, throttle disable) based on rider location. The Drover Corral dashboard surfaces real-time compliance insights and validation to operators and cities in line with the MDS 2.0 standard, delivered via API and automated Slack alerts. Partners and customers include Spin, Voi, Bolt, Beam, Dott, and Felyx. Drover AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published; integration is handled directly with operators.

providers.name: Explomar
providers.description: ExploMar (Changshu, China) designs and manufactures high-power fully-electric outboard propulsion systems for boats, ranging from 70HP to 1200HP. Its product line spans lightweight axial-flux electric outboard motors, high-density marine batteries for long-range and wide-temperature operation, the Smart Captain integrated control system with 200+ diagnostic capabilities, and 5S energy/charging stations (7kW portable through 120kW dual-gun). ExploMar markets an eco-friendly, high-performance alternative to combustion marine propulsion and exhibits at international yachting festivals (Cannes, Monaco, Interboot, Polboat). Backed by DCM Ventures; surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Note: ExploMar is a marine hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time — this profile carries identity and web-property signals only.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Glydways
providers.description: Glydways is an autonomous urban-transit company building on-demand, high-capacity mobility networks that combine small self-driving electric vehicles (Glydcars), an AI fleet-orchestration layer, and dedicated narrow guideways separated from regular road traffic. The system is designed to move up to 10,000 people per hour while cutting construction cost by roughly 90% and operating cost to about 30% of conventional transit, with launch projects underway in Atlanta, Contra Costa County, California, and at San Jose Airport. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Glydways was surfaced through the venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As an autonomous-transit infrastructure company it publishes a corporate and news presence but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: GoOpti
providers.description: GoOpti is a European ground-transportation marketplace for affordable airport transfers and intercity rides, connecting travelers with a network of vetted, contractual transport partners. Founded in Slovenia, GoOpti offers both shared (door-to-door pooled) and private transfers across Central and Southern Europe, using dynamic pricing where earlier, more flexible bookings earn lower fares. The company operates as a platform intermediary rather than a fleet owner, and has served more than two million passengers. Alongside its consumer booking site it runs B2B partner programs for agencies and resellers, corporate business accounts, franchising, and affiliates. GoOpti is a portfolio company of Point Nine and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, or agent-facing surface has been identified at this time.

providers.name: HelperGo
providers.description: HelperGo is a Hong Kong-based on-demand home services marketplace that connects households with more than 5,000 vetted local helpers for domestic cleaning, air-conditioning and window cleaning, cooking, childcare and babysitting, postnatal doula and confinement care, elderly and nursing care, and medical escort services. Customers book through the HelperGo iOS and Android apps or the website, with instant helper matching, ratings and reviews, and a satisfaction guarantee. HelperGo is a portfolio company of 500 Global and operates across Hong Kong and Singapore. The company is a consumer-facing service marketplace and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Jago Coffee
providers.description: Jago Coffee is an Indonesian mobile coffee company operating a fleet of electric-vehicle coffee carts ("Jagoans") that bring freshly brewed specialty coffee, tea, and seasonal drinks directly to neighborhoods across Indonesia. Billing itself as the "#1 Cafe on Wheels," Jago lets customers order through its mobile app with no delivery fees or order minimums, paying with GoPay or OVO digital wallets, using Arabica beans sourced directly from local Indonesian farmers. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer coffee-delivery business; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Kango
providers.description: Kango is an on-demand rides and childcare platform for families, connecting parents and schools with background-checked, fingerprinted drivers and sitters who transport and care for children from preschool through high school. Operated by Dolightful, Inc. and backed by 500 Global, Kango offers prescheduled and same-day rides, real-time ride tracking, in-app communication with drivers, provided car and booster seats, in-home sitter sessions, and a free carpool feature promoted by schools and camps. It runs on iOS and Android apps using a subscription plus per-ride and per-session fee model. Kango is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: LawnStarter
providers.description: LawnStarter is an on-demand lawn care and outdoor-services marketplace founded in 2013 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, that connects homeowners with vetted local lawn care professionals ("LawnTrepreneurs"). Beyond recurring lawn mowing, the platform books more than 30 services including landscaping, lawn treatments and fertilization, tree care, gutter cleaning, pressure washing, and leaf removal, with transparent online quoting, consistent crews, and a re-mow-or-refund quality guarantee. LawnStarter operates across 500+ cities, has served more than 500,000 customers through roughly 7,500 professionals, and reached profitability in 2021. LawnStarter runs a consumer web/mobile marketplace and a separate provider app (pros.lawnstarter.com); it does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Metro Africa Xpress
providers.description: Metro Africa Xpress (MAX), operating as maxdrive.ai, is a Nigerian technology-driven mobility company on a mission to make transportation safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable across Africa. MAX finances and deploys vehicles — including electric two- and three-wheelers — to a vetted network of driver-partners ("champions"), and runs a drivers services platform, electric-vehicle assembly and charging infrastructure, enterprise last-mile logistics, and mobility gov-tech solutions. Emerging from the MIT and Techstars ecosystem, MAX is backed by Novastar Ventures, Goodwell, Shell Foundation, Breakthrough Energy, Capria and Yamaha, and operates across Nigeria, Cameroon and other West African markets. The company publishes a marketing and corporate website only; no public developer program, API, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Moj.io
providers.description: Mojio (moj.io) is a connected-car and connected-mobility platform that collects, processes, and monetizes vehicle telematics data at scale for mobile network operators, automotive OEMs, insurers, and fleet/field-service businesses. Its "Mobility Studio" platform exposes REST endpoints for vehicle data, a PUSH API for real-time insights, mobile SDKs, and a vehicle simulator, alongside a white-label consumer app (Motion) and a services ecosystem (Alexa, Google Maps, Bosch, and others). Mojio has processed 15+ billion miles of driving data. As of this pass the API and SDK surface is partner-gated — there is no public developer portal, published OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Neuron Mobility
providers.description: Neuron Mobility is a rental e-scooter and e-bike operator and micromobility technology developer running shared micromobility fleets in cities across Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada. The company designs its own vehicles (including the N3 e-scooter), safety systems such as its patented Helmet Lock and ScootSafe rider training program, and the backend fleet-management, IoT, and geofencing technology that powers its rider apps and city operations. Backed by 500 Global, Neuron was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no first-party developer API, GBFS data feed, or well-known discovery surface on its own domain; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Preteckt
providers.description: Preteckt provides AI-powered predictive maintenance for transit buses, coach buses, and trucking fleets. Its platform ingests vehicle sensor telemetry and applies machine-learning algorithms to detect maintenance issues before they cause breakdowns, reducing diagnostic time by nearly 50 percent and preventing roughly 20 percent of failures. Preteckt processes more than one million sensor data points per day per vehicle across 20+ maintenance-focused algorithms. The company is part of Diesel Laptops. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Preteckt publishes no public developer, API, documentation, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: Rapido
providers.description: Rapido is an Indian on-demand urban mobility platform that connects riders with independent driver-partners (called "Captains") for bike taxis, auto rickshaws, and cabs through its consumer and Captain mobile apps. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by Accel, Rapido operates across hundreds of Indian cities and has expanded into parcel delivery and corporate mobility. As of this enrichment pass Rapido exposes only a consumer-facing web and app surface — no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification was found. This profile captures the company identity, its published policy and content pages, and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: ShiftSouth
providers.description: ShiftSouth (Pty) Ltd operates SweepSouth, South Africa's first on-demand home services marketplace, launched in 2014. The platform connects roughly 250,000 customers with about 6,500 vetted home-services professionals ("SweepStars") across Cape Town, Johannesburg, Sandton, Centurion, Pretoria, Durban, Umhlanga, Stellenbosch, Paarl and other South African cities. Services span on-demand and express indoor cleaning, office and Airbnb turnover cleaning, laundry and ironing, elder care, Mom's Helper and childcare, dog walking, gardening and pool maintenance, plus full-time placements of housekeepers, nannies and carers and a MyHome Hub subscription for managing private domestic workers. Professionals are background-checked, reference-verified and insured. SweepSouth is a 500 Global portfolio company and has won the Forbes Africa Women Innovation Award (2020) and the World Economic Forum Breakthrough Female Innovators Award (2017). It is a consumer marketplace with mobile apps for iOS and Android and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Shohoz
providers.description: Shohoz (Shohoj Limited) is a Bangladeshi consumer technology platform and digital super-app, billed as Bangladesh's largest online ticket destination. Founded in 2014 as an online ticketing service, it lets users book bus, train, air, launch (ferry), event, and movie tickets from its website and mobile apps, and expanded into ride-hailing (car and motorbike), on-demand delivery, and other everyday services. The company reports 10M+ users, 250M+ tickets sold, and 1,000+ transport and merchant partners across 3,000+ routes. Shohoz is a technology-first business but does not publish a public developer program, API reference, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SOLS Energy
providers.description: SOLS Energy is Malaysia's leading residential and commercial solar energy company, on a mission to make green energy a basic human right. It has completed more than 8,900 solar installations across Malaysia spanning residential (Green Homes), commercial (Green Business), and off-grid indigenous community projects (Green Impact), and also offers EV charging (ChargeSingh) and a Solar Academy apprenticeship program. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass SOLS Energy publishes a consumer marketing website (blog, FAQ, contact, privacy and terms pages) but no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Swift Charge
providers.description: Swift Charge is an electric vehicle charging company that provides turn-key, fully managed EV charging infrastructure to property owners across the hospitality, education, and multi-family residential sectors, pairing installed charging hardware with a payment application that lets EV drivers locate and pay for charging sessions. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Swift Charge publishes a public marketing and charger-map website but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile is limited to company identity plus a domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: Tiger New Energy
providers.description: Tiger New Energy is a Bangladesh-based clean-energy company building a battery-swapping network for electric vehicles, primarily electric rickshaws and motorcycles. Drivers swap depleted lithium batteries for fully charged ones at Tiger swapping stations in seconds instead of waiting to recharge, and a "battery passport" tracks each pack's health and lifecycle. The company operates consumer and partner mobile apps (Tiger Driver, Tiger Partner, Tiger Dealer) on iOS and Android. Tiger New Energy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its mobile apps are backed by private, undocumented services.

providers.name: Fleetline
providers.description: Fleetline is an all-in-one AI dispatch and fleet-optimization platform for trucking fleets. Its AI-based dispatch engine ingests load, driver, and ELD data, simulates billions of scenarios, and recommends the best assignment plan so operators maximize revenue, productivity, and fleet utilization. The platform aggregates major load boards into a unified workspace, identifies schedule gaps and fills them with spot loads, composes complex trips with tradeoff analysis, forecasts delays, breakdowns, and HOS violations, and includes an AI assistant trained on fleet history and TMS data. Fleetline is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it exposes a marketing site, a customer login/auth portal, and an internal API host, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Justos
providers.description: Justos is a Brazilian digital auto insurance insurtech founded in 2020 and headquartered in Barueri, São Paulo. Operating as a managing general agent (MGA), Justos uses smartphone-collected driving data (telematics) to reward safe drivers with lower, usage-based pricing — advertised as up to 30% cheaper than traditional plans — plus weekly bonuses and perks like gas vouchers, maintenance, and ride credits. Its products are distributed digitally through a consumer mobile app and a broker (corretor) portal, with claims tracked in-app and 24/7 support. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Kaszek, SoftBank Latin America and GGV; its auto insurance is underwritten by Companhia Excelsior de Seguros (SUSEP code 05690). No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: 24M
providers.description: 24M Technologies is a battery technology company founded in 2010 out of MIT laboratories and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rather than manufacturing cells at scale itself, 24M licenses its battery materials, cell architecture and SemiSolid manufacturing platform to energy-storage system integrators, EV battery manufacturers and OEMs worldwide. Its product portfolio spans the Eternalyte electrolyte (ultra-fast charging and low-temperature performance), the Impervio separator (thermal-runaway prevention), the LiForever electrode, the 24M ETOP electrode-to-pack architecture, and 24M production equipment. Partners and corporate investors have included Volkswagen Group, Kyocera, Itochu and FREYR Battery. 24M is a hardware, materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AirGarage
providers.description: AirGarage is a full-service parking management platform that helps property owners operate their parking lots and garages as revenue-generating real estate assets. The company combines proprietary data, full-service operations, and proactive pricing strategy: license plate recognition and aerial cameras capture real-time occupancy and compliance data, dynamic pricing automatically adjusts rates based on demand, aggregator marketing lists spaces across channels, on-the-ground teams handle real-time enforcement, and a managed driver-support operation processes mobile payments. Property owners get a real-time dashboard with transparency into revenue, occupancy, and market trends, on a revenue-share model with no long-term contracts. AirGarage is a portfolio company of a16z.

providers.name: Kopperfield
providers.description: Kopperfield is a software company building design and permitting tools for electrical contractors, electricians, inspectors and instructors. Founded in 2022, the company started as an EV charger installation booking service and has since become a broader contractor platform whose stated mission is to "accelerate home electrification by giving contractors the tools they need to work faster, smarter, and with total confidence." The web and mobile product covers NEC-compliant residential and commercial load calculations, drag-and-drop single line diagrams, panel schedules with circuit directories, AI panel-photo analysis, and a National Electrical Code chatbot trained on the 2017, 2020 and 2023 code editions. Kopperfield publishes a public llms.txt and a public status page but does not currently operate a public developer program: there is no published API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, and robots.txt disallows crawling of /api/. The company is backed by General Catalyst, MCJ Collective, Lachy Groom and Designer Fund.

providers.name: Motorq
providers.description: Motorq is a connected vehicle intelligence platform that taps native OEM connectivity to deliver AI-powered insights across the automotive ecosystem. It aggregates and normalizes vehicle telematics data from 25+ automotive brands and third-party sources without plug-in hardware or dongles, so fleets, fleet management companies, dealerships, lenders, insuretechs, and mobility companies can drive maintenance, safety, utilization, and EV use cases. Motorq offers access through a cloud fleet management portal, bi-directional APIs and data streams (Get Location, Create Geofence, and more), and a Snowflake data lake integration. Its Motorq Fuse AI layer surfaces prioritized recommendations ranked by severity and cost impact. API access is gated to enterprise and OEM partners; there is no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Pronto
providers.description: Pronto is an on-demand and subscription-based house-help marketplace operating across 11 Indian cities (including Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Hyderabad, and Pune). It connects urban homes with trained, background-verified Pronto Professionals for everyday household chores such as cleaning, laundry, kitchen prep, bathroom care, ironing, dusting, and window cleaning. Customers book in the Pronto mobile app (iOS and Android) for instant (a Pro in ~15 minutes), scheduled, or recurring service, and pay in-app; the withpronto.com website is the marketing surface while the booking flow runs in the app. Pronto is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; the only machine-readable surface is a provider-published llms.txt.

providers.name: Redwood Materials
providers.description: Redwood Materials is a Carson City, Nevada battery materials company founded in 2017 by former Tesla CTO JB Straubel. It operates a domestic circular supply chain for lithium-ion batteries: collecting and recycling end-of-life EV, consumer, micromobility and stationary-storage batteries, refining the recovered lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper, and remanufacturing anode copper foil and cathode active material for North American cell producers. Through Redwood Energy it also deploys second-life battery energy storage systems for data centers and the grid. Redwood runs the Tahoe Campus in Northern Nevada, the Carolina Campus outside Charleston, South Carolina, and an R&D center in San Francisco, and works with Panasonic, Toyota, GM, BMW, VW/Audi, Rivian, Caterpillar, Isuzu and Lime. Redwood publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server; its only machine-facing surface is a gated AWS Cognito partner portal used by automotive dismantlers to price and sell end-of-life battery packs.

providers.name: ApniBus
providers.description: ApniBus is an India-based online bus ticket booking platform that lets travelers search routes, compare operators, select seats, and pay for tickets across government and private bus services. It positions itself as a leading Indian bus-booking marketplace and an official RSRTC (Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation) booking partner, aggregating over one lakh bus services across thousands of routes. The consumer experience spans a website and Android/iOS apps, with UPI, cards, net banking, and wallet payments, instant e-ticket / m-ticket confirmation, live bus tracking, and easy cancellation. ApniBus was surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer or API program at this time.

providers.name: FordPass / Ford Pro
providers.description: FordPass is Ford Motor Company's consumer connected-vehicle mobile app and service platform for Ford and Lincoln owners, exposing remote start/stop, remote lock/unlock, vehicle status (fuel/charge, tire pressure, oil life, odometer, location), Vehicle Health alerts, BlueCruise hands-free driving, Wi-Fi hotspot, Phone As A Key, scheduled service, and roadside assistance via the embedded FordPass Connect 4G LTE modem. Ford Pro is Ford's commercial fleet brand spanning Ford Pro Telematics, Ford Pro Intelligence, Ford Pro E-Telematics for EVs, Ford Pro Charging, Ford Pro FinSimple, and dealer/upfit services. The Ford Developer Marketplace (developer.ford.com) hosts Ford's partner-facing API program — FordConnect Query API for consumer-vehicle data and remote command access (with vehicle-owner consent via FordPass account OAuth), plus a Ford Pro REST API surface for fleets including Vehicle Status, Vehicle Historical Status, Vehicle Metadata, Vehicle Efficiency (fuel/energy/idle), Driver Behavior, Trip Reports, and Vehicle Health. Ford Pro Telematics is integrated with Geotab, Fleetio, Samsara, Motive, Verizon Connect, and other fleet platforms, and Smartcar offers a consumer OAuth bridge to Ford vehicles using FordPass Connect credentials. Access to Ford APIs is gated behind a partner application and credentials issued through the Ford Developer Portal; Ford has periodically restricted individual-developer access. No public OpenAPI specification is published outside the partner portal, so this profile documents the Ford developer surface as an index without a generated machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Karnott
providers.description: Karnott is a French agricultural technology company based in Lille that builds connected tracking devices and a digital management platform for farms, equipment cooperatives (CUMA), agricultural contractors (ETA), and wine growers. Its beacon automatically records equipment usage and field interventions without manual data entry, enabling real-time fleet and equipment monitoring, fuel-cost tracking, parcel mapping, and precise billing and regulatory documentation. Karnott is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found on the provider's public surface as of this pass.

providers.name: MagicBus
providers.description: MagicBus is a vanpool management platform that helps employers, HR teams, fleet managers, and transit agencies rebuild and operate employee commuting programs. Through its MagicRide app, riders, drivers, and coordinators book seats, form dynamic on-demand vanpools, and crowdsource new routes, while reporting dashboards supply the data needed for program evaluation and transit-subsidy applications. Surfaced as a mobility portfolio lead of Version One Ventures and Y Combinator, MagicBus publishes no public API or developer program at this time; this profile captures its verified public web surface.

providers.name: NNG
providers.description: NNG (NNG Software Developing and Commercial LLC), formerly Nav N Go, is a Budapest-based automotive navigation and location-based software company founded in 2004. Its flagship iGO platform delivers modular guidance, positioning, routing, map content management, and driver-assistance features such as Intelligent Speed Assistance, embedded in more than 60 million devices across 30+ vehicle brands and supplied to over 150 automotive and mobility partners in nearly 200 countries. NNG is backed by growth investment from Insight Partners. NNG sells embedded and OEM location-based software rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: PitPro Automation
providers.description: PitPro Automation is a fleet-maintenance technology company building automated tire-service systems that perform full tire changes and rotations on commercial fleet vehicles in under fifteen minutes. Targeting Class 2 and smaller vehicles, the company serves last-mile delivery, rideshare, utility, telecom, moving, and government fleets with in-bay automation, 24/7 monitoring, and field support. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, PitPro is a hardware-and-software provider focused on reducing fleet downtime; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Poppy
providers.description: Poppy (poppyflowers.com) is an online, full-service wedding florist that designs, delivers, and sets up personalized floral arrangements for weddings across multiple US locations. Couples receive a custom floral proposal based on their style preferences, with bridal and bridesmaid bouquets, boutonnieres, ceremony installations, arches, reception centerpieces, and table arrangements, all delivered and installed on-site by Poppy's team. The company publishes pricing guidance (a $1,750 order minimum, ~$3,400 average spend, a $249 deposit to secure dates) and offers interest-free monthly payment plans and flexible modifications up to 60 days before the event. Poppy was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Poppy operates a consumer-facing website only and publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Getaround
providers.description: Getaround was a peer-to-peer and connected car-sharing marketplace (merged with France's Drivy in 2019) that let owners list personal or fleet vehicles fitted with Getaround Connect - a BLE/telematics smart-lock kit - for keyless, app-based rental. Getaround historically ran a documented Owner API and webhook program for fleet-management partners (CarSync, FleetWire, Invers Fleet Hawk) plus a native Connect Blueforce BLE SDK for lock/unlock. OPERATING STATUS (as of 2026-07-03) - the company is winding down - it shut down U.S. operations (including its HyreCar subsidiary) in February 2025, sold its European car-sharing business to Denmark's GoMore ApS effective April 30, 2026, and Getaround Inc.'s board voted June 5, 2026 to pursue formal Delaware dissolution and liquidation (stockholder vote July 29, 2026, no distribution expected). The api.getaround.com API host no longer resolves and its owner API documentation page is now empty, so the API described here is historical/discontinued rather than currently operable.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: Rivian Automotive
providers.description: Rivian Automotive is an American electric vehicle manufacturer that designs and builds adventure-oriented electric trucks, SUVs, and commercial delivery vans, along with the charging infrastructure and connected-vehicle software that supports them. While Rivian does not publish a public developer API portal, an unofficial GraphQL API powers the Rivian mobile app and has been reverse-engineered by community projects for vehicle telemetry and control.

providers.name: Voya
providers.description: Voya GmbH is a software development and consulting company based in Hamburg, Germany, with nearshore TechHubs in Bucharest and Cluj, Romania. Founded in 2015 as an AI-powered chat-based business-travel booking platform backed by 500 Global, it became a wholly-owned Volkswagen Group subsidiary and has been an independent, founder-led company again since November 2024. Today Voya delivers end-to-end software development, applied AI solutions, and engineering team building for automotive, mobility, and travel clients including Volkswagen, Audi, CARIAD, Deutsche Bahn, and Lufthansa City Center. TISAX certified. Voya publishes no public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Circle K
providers.description: Circle K is a global convenience store and fuel station chain operating more than 14,800 stores worldwide including 9,799 locations in North America and 2,697 in Europe across 48 U.S. states and over 30 countries. A subsidiary of Alimentation Couche-Tard, Circle K operates the Inner Circle Rewards loyalty program, the Easy Pay fuel payment system, an EV charging network, and the Circle K PRO Business Fleet Card.

providers.name: Rabbit Mobility
