Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.

providers.name: Drivezy
providers.description: Drivezy — founded in Bengaluru, India in 2015 and originally launched as JustRide — operated a peer-to-peer vehicle-sharing and self-drive rental marketplace covering cars, motorcycles and scooters, pairing a company-operated fleet with vehicles listed by individual owners. It raised venture funding through a Series B and held acquisition talks with Yamaha. Drivezy never ran a public developer program: no portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract were ever published. The /api/* endpoints visible in archived captures of secure.drivezy.com were the private backend of its consumer mobile app. As of 2026-08-12 drivezy.com does not resolve: the registry still delegates it to Cloudflare nameservers, but those nameservers answer REFUSED, so every lookup returns SERVFAIL. The domain had already left the company before it went dark — Internet Archive captures show the real site through mid-2024, a bare WordPress shell through 2025, and unrelated Indonesian gambling SEO spam from December 2025 until the final capture on 2026-05-11 — so a drivezy.com that resolves again should not be read as this company without fresh evidence. What remains public is the github.com/drivezy organization and thirteen packages on Packagist and npm — internal Laravel and JavaScript platform libraries, not API client SDKs.

providers.name: Alba Robot
providers.description: ALBA Robot is a Turin, Italy based autonomous micro-mobility company building a fleet of self-driving robots for indoor and pedestrian spaces such as airports, hospitals, and large facilities. Its product line includes ALBA One, ALBA Ride, ALBA Ride +, and the ALBA Caddie autonomous baggage transport robot, and it layers digital services such as Digital Twins and Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) advertising on top of the mobility platform. ALBA Robot runs pilots and deployments with airports including Cagliari, London Gatwick, Dallas, Milan, Turin, and Dubai (with dnata), and operates from Turin with a US presence in Detroit, Michigan. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization; it is a hardware/robotics fleet operator rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Anda
providers.description: Anda (andaafrica.com) is an Angolan mobility and delivery company that operates ride-hailing and courier services using motorcycles, electric motorcycles, and tuk-tuks, integrating technology, finance, and sustainability to serve people and businesses across Angola. Anda runs a drive-to-own model that empowers drivers to own their vehicles through training (ANDA Academia), insurance, maintenance support, and safe operating hubs, turning informal transport work into stable livelihoods. Moto-taxi rides are fulfilled through the Yango app, alongside green electric-motorcycle options, tuk-tuk transport, and express delivery. The company is based in Talatona, Angola, and is a portfolio company of Speedinvest (invested 2025). Anda does not currently publish any public API or developer documentation; this profile captures the verified company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Culdesac
providers.description: Culdesac is a post-car real estate development company building walkable, car-free neighborhoods in the United States. Its first project, Culdesac Tempe in Tempe, Arizona, broke ground in 2019 and welcomed its first residents in 2021 — a 16-acre, roughly $140 million development of 636 apartment units plus 24,000 square feet of restaurant and retail space, designed with no resident parking. Residents receive transportation benefits such as free light-rail rides and discounted rideshare and scooter access in place of car ownership. Culdesac operates leasing, tours, and resident services through its website and HubSpot-backed portals, and intends to replicate the car-free neighborhood model in other cities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Culdesac publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Esar
providers.description: Esar (ايسار) is a Saudi Arabia and UAE based car rental marketplace that connects vehicle owners with renters through a mobile app, offering luxury, sports, family, and 4x4 vehicles across Riyadh, Jeddah, Mecca, and Dubai. The platform lets car owners list vehicles to earn recurring returns while giving travelers on-demand access to a curated fleet at competitive daily rates. Headquartered in Jeddah, Esar is an early-stage startup backed by 500 Global and the Taqadam accelerator. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Floward
providers.description: Floward is a leading online flowers and luxury gifting company headquartered in Kuwait and operating across the Middle East and the United Kingdom. Founded in 2017, the company delivers fresh flower arrangements, curated gift boxes, chocolates, cakes, and personalized gifts to more than 40 cities across 9 countries, sourcing blooms daily from ethical growers worldwide and offering same-day and scheduled delivery through its web store and mobile apps. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: JD Logistics
providers.description: JD Logistics (Hong Kong listed as 2618.HK) is a technology-driven supply chain and logistics service provider spun out of JD.com and backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates one of China's largest integrated logistics networks, offering express and freight delivery, integrated warehouse-and-fulfillment, cold-chain and pharmaceutical logistics, cross-border shipping, oversized-item handling, and smart supply-chain technology. Through its JD Logistics Open Platform (open.jdl.com) it exposes enterprise integration services for order fulfillment, warehousing, waybill/shipment creation, tracking, and reconciliation to merchants and partners. This profile tracks the company's public developer and open-platform surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: omio
providers.description: Omio (formerly GoEuro) is a Berlin-based travel booking platform that lets travelers search, compare, and book trains, buses, ferries, and flights across thousands of transport providers throughout Europe and beyond from a single website and mobile app. Founded in 2013 as GoEuro and rebranded to Omio in 2019, the company aggregates schedules, fares, and seat availability from hundreds of carriers into one checkout. Omio does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its carrier and distribution integrations are handled through private B2B partnerships. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched by probing Omio's public domain, DNS, and security surface.

providers.name: Spotangels
providers.description: SpotAngels is a consumer parking application that helps drivers find free and cheap parking, understand and avoid confusing street-parking rules, get reminders before street cleaning and permit-zone changes, and book discounted garage and lot parking in major cities. The company also runs business programs for cities, universities, and parking operators/owners to surface availability and deals. SpotAngels is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; its integrations are business partnerships rather than developer-facing APIs.

providers.name: Autonomic
providers.description: Autonomic is a connected-vehicle cloud company founded in 2016, acquired by Ford Motor Company in 2018 and fully integrated into Ford in 2023. Its flagship product, the Transportation Mobility Cloud (TMC), is one of the largest connected-vehicle cloud platforms in production, providing an API-driven platform for developers to build applications that interact with vehicles while abstracting the complexity of different vehicle models and connectivity devices. The public developer surface (the TMC Developer Portal) is gated behind partner authentication, so most technical artifacts are not publicly harvestable. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Craft Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Onramp Payments
providers.description: Onramp Payments, Inc. (ONRAMP) is a fintech company building modern payments infrastructure for the commercial trucking and fleet industry. Founded by logistics and payments veterans and backed by Canaan Partners, the company operates an enterprise-grade digital platform that replaces legacy card-based fleet payment systems. For carriers it offers cardless fuel payments at the pump, administrative spend controls, and maintenance payment solutions; for merchants it provides digital payment acceptance, pricing controls, and fraud prevention that work both in-store and at fuel pumps; and for partners it offers API integrations, broker solutions, and Transportation Management System (TMS) connections. The company markets itself as the easiest, most secure payments platform for carriers and merchants and has raised roughly $21M from investors including Canaan Partners, CEAS Investments, Contour Venture Partners, Javelin Venture Partners, and RedBlue Capital. As of this enrichment pass ONRAMP publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures verified company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: AssetWorks
providers.description: AssetWorks is an enterprise fleet and asset management software company with more than 40 years of history and over 1,000 customers across commercial and private fleets, government and public works, and higher education. Its products include FleetFocus fleet and enterprise asset management (EAM), Active Assets fixed-asset tracking, Recoup Ops surplus management, and Scan and Validate mobile inventory management. AssetWorks sells on-premise and hosted enterprise software to large fleet and facility operators; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve API program. This repo is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Awfar Market
providers.description: Awfar is a Cairo- and Riyadh-based digital solutions company (founded 2013) offering an integrated customer engagement and commerce platform. It combines an omnichannel Chat Center with AI agents (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook), a cloud Call Center, and a Commerce & Delivery platform for order, inventory, and logistics management within a single interface. Awfar serves more than 2,000 clients across retail, pharmacy, restaurant, e-commerce, tourism, healthcare, education, and real estate, and ships prebuilt integrations for Shopify, Meta, Odoo, Zid, and Salla plus custom API connections. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; integration is arranged via the sales and demo channel.

providers.name: Drivemate
providers.description: Drivemate is a peer-to-peer car-sharing and car-rental marketplace based in Bangkok, Thailand, founded in 2016. The platform lets vehicle owners list their cars and lets travelers and residents rent directly from those owners through the Drivemate mobile app and website, handling booking, verification, insurance and payments end to end. Drivemate operates one of the largest car-rental selections in Thailand with more than 3,000 vehicles across 35 provinces and a community of over 100,000 users, and has raised Series A funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), NetSol, Isuzu UNT and Colopl Next. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public digital and developer surface; Drivemate is a consumer mobility marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API program, so this record captures identity, distribution and domain-security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Fluid Truck
providers.description: Fluid Truck was a Denver, Colorado peer-to-peer commercial vehicle sharing platform founded in 2016 by James Eberhard and Jenifer Snyder, often described as "the Zipcar of commercial vehicles". It operated an app-based, self-service rental marketplace for cargo vans, box trucks and flatbeds across roughly 400 cities in 32 US states, and ran the Fluid Vehicle Investor Program (FVIP) through which individuals and small businesses bought fleets that Fluid managed and rented out. The company raised over $80 million in venture funding, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware in October 2024 after an $20.6 million cash loss in 2023, sold substantially all assets to Kingbee Rentals in December 2024, and the case converted to Chapter 7 liquidation in September 2025. The company is wound down: no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract was ever published, and its own web properties no longer serve a valid TLS certificate.

providers.name: GreenQ
providers.description: GreenQ is an Israeli smart waste-management technology company (founded 2015, Jerusalem) promoting the "Internet of Garbage" — turning ordinary garbage trucks into smart trucks. Its GreenTrack device installs on any collection vehicle to weigh incoming waste and track route, mileage, capacity, time and per-bin (single-can-level) pickup data without requiring sensors on the bins, using a patent-pending visual-recognition algorithm. A recommendations engine then suggests route-optimization and scheduling improvements, surfaced through the GreenQ dashboard of reports and analytics. Collected data can be integrated with a municipality's local-authority systems through a private integration API; the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or specification. GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kitchensurfing
providers.description: Kitchensurfing was a New York City marketplace that booked professional chefs to shop for, cook, and serve meals in customers' own kitchens, founded in 2012 and backed by roughly $20M from Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, and Tiger Global. It began as an advance-booking platform for private dinner parties and pivoted in 2015 to a flat-rate on-demand model in which a chef arrived and cooked dinner within a fixed window. Neither model produced sustainable demand against better-capitalized meal-kit and delivery competitors, and the company discontinued service and shut down on April 15, 2016. It never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Its GitHub organization survives with eleven public repositories - open-source Ruby/Rails forks and internal hackathon projects, last active in 2016 - but contains no client library or API definition. The kitchensurfing.com domain was subsequently re-registered by an unrelated cooking-products affiliate publisher and no longer represents this company.

providers.name: Lori Systems
providers.description: Lori Systems is a Nairobi-headquartered, pan-African digital freight platform that matches cargo owners with vetted transporters to coordinate long-haul trucking across the continent. Founded in 2016 by Josh Sandler, Jean-Claude Homawoo, and Ernest Gichini Ngaruiya, the company is now led by CEO Uche Ogboi and runs operations from offices in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, moving cargo across roughly 12 African countries with a network of 20,000+ trucks and over $10B of cargo facilitated. The platform offers shippers instant rate estimates, load matching, real-time shipment tracking, electronic proof of delivery, and integrated payments, while giving transporters access to cargo orders, truck-availability management, and prompt payment on delivery. Lori operates a public rate-card tool at ratecard.lorisystems.com, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification; its GitHub organization is limited to small internal-tooling repositories (a Singer.io tap for Freshsales, a BambooHR Python client, a Kubernetes Terraform provider, and similar utilities) rather than a customer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Chemix
providers.description: Chemix is an artificial-intelligence company building an end-to-end, AI-enabled power system for batteries, organized around the themes of power safety, observability, and predictability. Based in Sunnyvale, California, the company applies generative and machine-learning techniques to make battery behavior more transparent and predictable across the battery lifecycle. Chemix is a Mayfield-backed portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this profile the company is pre-launch ("more product details coming soon") and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this record captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Parkhub
providers.description: Parkhub provided parking management and payment processing APIs for parking operators and venues. Parkhub has been acquired and the parkhub.com domain now redirects to JustPark Business. Public API documentation is no longer available.

providers.name: BorgWarner
providers.description: BorgWarner is a global automotive supplier designing and manufacturing propulsion systems, thermal management, battery systems, charging solutions, and power electronics for combustion, hybrid, and electric vehicles. The company accelerates the world's transition to clean, efficient mobility across passenger and commercial vehicle markets.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Movel AI
providers.description: Movel AI is a Singapore-based robotics deployment software company, founded in 2016, that makes it faster and cheaper to get autonomous mobile robots up and running in real-world environments. Its platform pairs deep learning, sensor fusion, and probabilistic planning so robots can perceive their surroundings and plan tasks on their own. Core products are the Movel Fleet Management System (FMS) for real-time monitoring and control of multi-robot fleets and Movel RNS (Robotic Navigation System) for precise single-robot navigation of complex spaces, applied across logistics, manufacturing, construction, and healthcare. The company is backed by Silicon Solution Ventures, 500 Global, AviTech, SGInnovate, Seeds Capital, and Enterprise Singapore. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Movel AI publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Rappi
providers.description: Rappi is a Colombian-founded pan-Latin American super-app headquartered in Bogotá, with regional hubs in São Paulo and Mexico City. Founded in 2015 by Simón Borrero, Sebastián Mejía, and Felipe Villamarín, and accelerated through Y Combinator's W16 batch, Rappi operates across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and Uruguay. The platform bundles on-demand delivery (restaurants, groceries via "Súper" and Turbo Fresh, pharmacies, retail, alcohol) with consumer fintech (RappiPay, RappiCard, RappiCash) and adjacent services such as RappiTravel and the RappiPrime subscription. Rappi's developer surface is operated through its Partners program at dev-portal.rappi.com, where approved restaurants, retailers, and middleware providers obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials to integrate with a REST API for menu and catalog management, store availability, order lifecycle events, financial reconciliation, and webhook subscriptions. Access is not self-serve — a Rappi business contact must approve onboarding, after which partners receive development-environment credentials and an integration path to production. SoftBank-backed since 2019, Rappi competes regionally with iFood, Uber Eats, and DiDi Food, with fintech ambitions overlapping Nubank, Mercado Pago, and regional neobanks.

providers.name: Rubicon
providers.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Swiftmile
providers.description: Swiftmile is a California-based hardware and IoT company building universal charging and parking infrastructure for micromobility — docking stations that power, secure and organize shared and privately owned e-bikes and e-scooters, including solar-powered units and integrated digital advertising panels. Founded around 2014 and headquartered on the San Francisco Peninsula, it supplied secure charging docks to the New York City DOT public e-bike charging pilot alongside PopWheels and Swobbee. Company interviews describe a fleet- and battery-management backend with integrations offered to micromobility operators, but Swiftmile has never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and as of 2026-08-29 swiftmile.com no longer serves the company website at all — the domain answers with a Nexcess hosting placeholder and a TLS certificate that does not match the hostname.

providers.name: Axalta Coating Systems
providers.description: Axalta Coating Systems is a global supplier of liquid and powder coatings for transportation and industrial end-markets, operating through Performance Coatings (refinish and industrial) and Mobility Coatings (light vehicle and commercial vehicle) segments. Brands include Cromax, Spies Hecker, Standox, Imron, and Voltatex. In July 2024 Axalta acquired The CoverFlexx Group from Transtar Holding for $285 million to expand its economy-tier aftermarket coverage in North America. In November 2025 Axalta announced a $17 billion all-stock merger of equals with AkzoNobel that is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, forming a coatings company with dual headquarters in Amsterdam and Philadelphia.

providers.name: Bestmile
providers.description: Bestmile was a Swiss fleet-orchestration SaaS company, spun out of EPFL in Lausanne in 2014, whose cloud platform planned, dispatched and optimized mixed fleets of autonomous and human-driven vehicles for on-demand mobility and transit operators. The platform was described by the company as API-first, with documented Fleet, Booking and Transportation APIs for integrating operator booking apps, fleet-management systems and traveler-information systems. The company no longer operates: ZF Friedrichshafen acquired Bestmile's technology in November 2021 and folded it into its own SCALAR fleet-orchestration platform, so any successor API belongs to ZF rather than to Bestmile. As of 2026-08-17 bestmile.com is a parked Gandi.net registrar domain that refuses HTTPS, and no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, package or /.well-known surface survives. Surfaced originally as a Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Boson Motors
providers.description: Boson Motors is an electric vehicle and robotics company founded in 2017, building a modular electric off-road utility vehicle (UTV) platform for agriculture, farm automation, and work applications. Its flagship LX40 is a user-serviceable, low-maintenance electric 4WD UTV that charges from a standard 110v outlet and accepts interchangeable work modules for spraying, hauling, and crew transport. The company operates engineering and production out of Tada, Andhra Pradesh, India, with a strategic base in Fremont, California, and maintains a robotics arm (Boson Robotics) focused on autonomous and agricultural automation. Boson Motors is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer marketing and reservation site with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation; its public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of ROS/robotics libraries. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and enrichment target.

providers.name: Kitchit
providers.description: Kitchit was a San Francisco on-demand private-chef marketplace founded in 2011 by Brendan Marshall and Ian Ferguson. The service matched consumers with vetted professional chefs who shopped, cooked, served, and cleaned up a multi-course meal in the customer's own home, booked through the kitchit.com web and mobile storefront. In 2015 the company pivoted from fully customized menus to a lower-priced standardized product marketed as "Kitchit Tonight," priced around $39 per person with a two-person minimum. Kitchit served more than 100,000 meals across roughly five years of operation and reported a net promoter score of 87. It raised approximately $8.1M, with investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Crosslink Capital, Javelin Venture Partners, and Otter Rock Capital. The company announced its shutdown in April 2016, with the founders citing a finite investment runway that ended amid broad upheaval in food-tech, alongside contemporaneous failures at SpoonRocket, Dinner Lab, and Kitchensurfing. Kitchit is defunct: it operates no website, developer portal, or public API today, and no public API surface was ever published. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record for network completeness.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Pep Boys
providers.description: Pep Boys is an American automotive aftermarket service chain founded in 1921 and headquartered in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania. Owned by Icahn Enterprises since 2016, Pep Boys completed its transition away from retail parts in December 2023 and now operates as a service-only chain with roughly 850 to 900+ service centers across the U.S. and Puerto Rico, including a Pep Boys Mobile Crew offering for fleet and on-location maintenance. Pep Boys does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Wheels Up
providers.description: Wheels Up Experience Inc. (NYSE: UP) is a leading on-demand private aviation provider in the U.S., offering charter and membership programs, commercial travel benefits through a strategic partnership with Delta Air Lines, and cargo services. Founded in 2013 by Kenny Dichter, Wheels Up was rescued from potential bankruptcy in September 2023 when a Delta Air Lines-led consortium (Delta, Certares, Knighthead, Cox) closed a $500M financing package and took a ~95% controlling equity stake. In November 2024 the company acquired the Embraer Phenom 300/300E fleet of GrandView Aviation ($105M) and secured $332M in equipment financing from Bank of America as part of a multi-year fleet modernization toward two core aircraft types (Phenom 300 series and Challenger 300/350). In 2025 it launched a new Signature membership portfolio and an industry-first integrated self-booking of Delta commercial flights inside the Wheels Up members app. Wheels Up does not publish a public developer API — its booking surface is a members-only mobile app and members.wheelsup.com web portal, with B2B operator connectivity historically routed through its acquired Avianis platform (2019).

providers.name: Quick Ride
providers.description: Quick Ride is an Indian mobility platform offering carpooling, bikepool, and taxi services across major cities including Bangalore, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, Kochi, NCR, and Chandigarh. Riders book airport, outstation, rental, and local trips across vehicle classes from hatchbacks to luxury SUVs, or share commutes via car and bike pooling to cut cost and congestion. The service is delivered through consumer iOS and Android apps. No public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP, SDKs) is published; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of prosus-ventures and enriched via live web and DNS/TLS probes.

providers.name: Ahlijasa
providers.description: Ahlijasa was an Indonesian on-demand home services startup founded in 2015 in the Greater Jakarta area by Jay Jayawijayaningtiyas and Made Dimas Astra Wijaya. It originally offered laundry, air-conditioning repair, and home cleaning before pivoting in late 2016 to focus exclusively on on-demand laundry by partnering with premium and traditional laundrettes to give them a digital storefront and online customer base. The company won Startup World Cup Indonesia in 2016 and raised seed funding in May 2017 from 500 Startups (500 Global), Fenox VC, and Indogen Capital, but secured no further funding afterward. Its primary domain (ahlijasa.com) now resolves to a domain-parking/for-sale page, indicating the business is no longer operating. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were found for this provider during enrichment.

providers.name: Alibaba Local Services
providers.description: Alibaba Local Services (阿里巴巴本地生活) is Alibaba Group's on-demand local-life services business, formed in 2018 by integrating the Ele.me food-delivery platform with the Koubei local-services and restaurant-discovery platform. It operates on-demand food and grocery delivery, local merchant services, reviews and reservations, and last-mile logistics across China, and received a major financing round led by the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the network as a lead; no distinct public developer API surface has been confirmed for the holding entity under this name (its consumer platforms Ele.me and Koubei operate their own separate open platforms).

providers.name: Anycart
providers.description: Anycart is a consumer grocery delivery and store-pickup platform that lets shoppers enter a zip code, choose a favorite local grocery store, and shop for anything they need with no price markups and no service fees. The service spans multiple U.S. retailers and focuses on transparent pricing for everyday grocery ordering, delivery, and pickup. Anycart was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates a consumer web and mobile storefront (anycart.com) and does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Automatic Labs
providers.description: Automatic Labs was a connected-car company (the Automatic OBD-II adapter and companion app plus a developer platform / REST API for trip, vehicle, and driving-behavior data), founded circa 2011 and backed by a16z. It was acquired by SiriusXM in 2017 and wound down: the service and its developer API were discontinued around May 2020. As of this enrichment pass the automatic.com domain (and its api./developer. subdomains) 301-redirects to automattic.com, the unrelated WordPress company, so no live API, documentation, or developer surface remains to harvest. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio lead.

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: Carpooling
providers.description: Carpooling.com GmbH was one of Europe's largest ridesharing / carpooling platforms, founded in Munich, Germany and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It connected drivers with empty seats to passengers travelling the same route across Europe. In April 2015 the company was acquired by the French ridesharing operator BlaBlaCar and its operations were merged into that platform. The carpooling.com domain and every developer-facing subdomain (developer / api / docs) now redirect to BlaBlaCar (blablacar.co.uk), and no independent Carpooling developer portal, API, or specification remains. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record; there is no live API surface of its own to enrich.

providers.name: Caviar
providers.description: Caviar is a premium restaurant food-ordering and delivery marketplace that connects diners with local, higher-end and popular restaurants for on-demand delivery and pickup. Originally launched in 2012 and later owned by Square, Caviar was acquired by DoorDash in 2019 and now operates on DoorDash's logistics and marketplace platform under the trycaviar.com brand. The service focuses on curated restaurant selection, quality-oriented ordering, courier delivery, and catering. Caviar does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and captures whatever public, agent-relevant surface exists.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Damon Motorcycles
providers.description: Damon Motorcycles (Damon Inc.) is a Vancouver, British Columbia electric motorcycle company founded in 2017 by Jay Giraud and Dominique Kwong, and an alumnus of the Techstars accelerator. Damon builds high-performance electric motorcycles led by the HyperSport and HyperFighter models, and is known for two safety and ergonomics technologies: CoPilot, a 360-degree advanced warning system that uses radar, cameras, and sensors to alert riders to surrounding hazards, and Shift, a transformable ergonomics system that adjusts the riding position between commuter and sport stances. The company has faced significant financial and going-concern difficulties, and its public web presence at damon.com currently returns errors, so no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be verified during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dingdong
providers.description: Dingdong (Dingdong Maicai / 叮咚买菜) is a Shanghai-based on-demand fresh-grocery e-commerce company operating a front-warehouse (dark-store) model that delivers fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and prepared foods to consumers, typically within about 30 minutes, through its mobile app. The company is publicly listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DDL) and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Its public surface (ddxq.mobi) is a consumer mobile-app backend rather than a developer platform; no public developer portal, API documentation, or open API program was found during enrichment, and the host is not reachable outside of China.

providers.name: Dolly
providers.description: Dolly was a Seattle-based on-demand moving and last-mile delivery marketplace that connected people who needed help moving furniture and large items with independent "Helpers" who owned pickup trucks and vans, coordinated through consumer and retail-partner mobile apps. It grew a same-day big-and-bulky delivery network used by retailers such as IKEA, Costco, Lowe's, West Elm, and Peloton. Dolly was acquired and folded into TaskRabbit (owned by IKEA / Ingka Group); as of 2026 the dolly.com domain 301-redirects entirely to taskrabbit.com/delivery, and the service now operates under the "Taskrabbit Delivery" brand. No standalone Dolly-owned developer portal, public API, or well-known discovery surface survives — every dolly.com path redirects into TaskRabbit. This profile records the honest disposition of the company; the developer/API footprint now lives (if anywhere) under TaskRabbit, not Dolly.

providers.name: Eaze
providers.description: Eaze is a California-based cannabis marketplace and delivery platform that connects licensed dispensaries and cannabis brands with adult consumers, offering online ordering and same-day delivery of flower, edibles, vapes, and related products across the state. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Francisco, Eaze operates a consumer marketplace plus a technology and logistics stack for compliant retail. Backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. Eaze does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its api.eaze.com host is an internal, bot-protected surface.

providers.name: FlightCar
providers.description: FlightCar was a United States peer-to-peer car-rental marketplace built around airport travel, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company behind the name and no API surface of any kind. The domain flightcar.com is registered but publishes no A, AAAA or MX records, resolves to no host, and sits on Njalla privacy nameservers with a SOA serial dated 2026-07-18; the api, developer and docs subdomains do not resolve; there is no GitHub organisation at github.com/flightcar; and no first-party client library exists on npm or PyPI. The Internet Archive shows the consumer site returning 200 through May 2016 and an Internal Server Error by July 2017, with no successful captures in 2017 or 2018. FlightCar is therefore carried in the network as a defunct company retained for portfolio-graph and historical continuity rather than as an active API provider, and should not be re-queued for artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Garaji
providers.description: Garaji was an online auto-services marketplace based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, founded in 2018, that connected car owners with local workshops for routine maintenance and repairs. Customers selected a service and a vetted garage, and a Garaji valet or tow truck collected the vehicle, delivered it to the workshop, and returned it once work was complete. Garaji was a 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) portfolio company. The company is permanently closed, and its domain garaji.com is now a parked, for-sale listing served via GoDaddy/Afternic with no live product or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no APIs or developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Gotiger
providers.description: GoTiger is a Berlin-based food company that operates multiple delivery-first food brands out of modern ghost kitchens, including Bok Bok Chicken, GoDumpling and Kyoo Chicken. Founded in 2022, the company began as GoTiger Asia Grocery Delivery, a same-day app-based service delivering Japanese, Korean and Chinese groceries and everyday essentials across Berlin and Potsdam on a Shopify Plus backend, before pivoting to a portfolio of virtual restaurant brands. GoTiger is a consumer product company backed by Speedinvest, Adjacent, Nucleus Capital and Shio Capital; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Hassle
providers.description: Hassle.com was a London-based on-demand home-cleaning marketplace, founded in 2012 by Alex Depledge and Jules Coleman, connecting households with vetted local cleaners for one-off and recurring bookings. Backed by Accel Partners, it was acquired by Rocket Internet-backed Helpling in July 2015 for a reported EUR 32 million to form one of the world's largest home-cleaning marketplaces. The Hassle.com brand was subsequently folded into Helpling, whose UK operations have since ceased; the domain now redirects to Helpling. The company operates a consumer-facing web/mobile booking product and exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: HeartyyFresh
providers.description: HeartyyFresh is a mobile-first Indian grocery delivery service that lets customers order fresh Indian groceries and household staples for home delivery through its iOS and Android apps. The consumer offering centers on convenience and quality, promoting a first-time incentive of 20% off the first five orders placed through the app. HeartyyFresh operates as a direct-to-consumer grocery app (published under the com.rahein.heartyyfresh Android package and the "HeartyyFresh - Indian Grocery" iOS listing) rather than a developer platform; it exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched for identity only.

providers.name: HomeJoy
providers.description: Homejoy, Inc. was an online home-services marketplace that connected customers with vetted house cleaners and handymen through its website and mobile apps. Founded in 2010 by siblings Adora and Aaron Cheung, the Y Combinator-backed company raised roughly $40M (Google Ventures, Redpoint, First Round, Max Levchin) and expanded to more than 30 cities across the US, UK, Canada, France and Germany. Battered by high customer churn, discount-driven growth and worker-misclassification lawsuits, Homejoy ceased operations on July 31, 2015; much of its product and engineering team was acqui-hired by Google. This is an archival API Evangelist profile of a defunct company: it operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its former homejoy.com domain now redirects to an unrelated cleaning service.

providers.name: Iomob
providers.description: Iomob (The Internet of Mobility) was a Barcelona-based Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) technology company founded in 2017. Its platform let cities, transport operators, and corporations orchestrate multimodal, door-to-door journeys — combining public transit, ride-hailing, taxis, micromobility, parking, and demand-responsive transport — through unified journey-planning APIs, native iOS/Android SDKs, and customizable white-label apps. Iomob's MaaS platform and SDK were acquired by Busup in January 2025 to build a corporate mobility platform; the Iomob UK entity was dissolved in September 2025 and the public website (iomob.net) is currently offline (Cloudflare 526 origin error). No public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK packages, or GitHub organization could be verified during enrichment — Iomob's APIs and SDKs were delivered under B2B/partner agreements.

providers.name: J&T Express
providers.description: J&T Express (J&T Global Express Ltd, HKEX: 1519) is a global logistics service operator whose core business is express parcel delivery and international logistics. Founded in Indonesia in 2015, it operates express delivery networks across 13 countries including Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Cambodia, Singapore, China, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Mexico, Brazil, and Egypt, with international freight services reaching Asia, Europe, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania. The company serves e-commerce sellers and consumers with parcel pickup, sorting, line-haul, last-mile delivery, and track-and-trace. As of this profile J&T Express publishes a public track-and-trace web experience and regional merchant onboarding, but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Kaodim
providers.description: Kaodim was a Southeast Asian on-demand home and local services marketplace founded in 2014 that connected consumers with service providers such as cleaners, plumbers, electricians, aircon technicians, movers, tutors, and event professionals. Headquartered in Malaysia, it operated regionally under Kaodim.com (Malaysia), Kaodim.sg (Singapore), Gawin.ph (Philippines), and Beres.id (Indonesia), and raised venture funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), Venturra Capital, and Square Peg. The company ceased all operations on July 1, 2022, citing prolonged COVID-19 lockdowns, labor shortages, rising costs, and weakened demand. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface exists for the defunct company, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Keno
providers.description: Keno is an on-demand, doorstep car-wash and vehicle-care mobile application operating in the United Arab Emirates, billing itself as the "No.1 car wash app in the UAE". Customers download the iOS or Android app, add their vehicle, select from wash, maintenance, and detailing services (priced by vehicle class from bike to luxury SUV), and a mobile team of "ninjas" arrives at the customer's location to perform the work with a choice of payment methods. Keno is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kubota Corporation
providers.description: Kubota Corporation is a Japanese multinational manufacturing agricultural, construction, and industrial machinery, including compact tractors, excavators, mowers, utility vehicles, engines, and water and environmental infrastructure systems sold in over 120 countries. Kubota does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; equipment telematics (KubotaNOW) and dealer integrations are handled through partner channels rather than open APIs.

providers.name: Kyte
providers.description: Kyte was a full-stack technology-operations company that delivered rental cars on demand to the customer's door, positioning itself for any trip longer than a rideshare — a car for a day, a few days, or longer — with no rental counters, no lines and no paperwork. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company combined a consumer mobile and web booking experience with its own fleet and delivery operations ("bits and atoms"), and at its peak operated in 14 US markets delivering tens of thousands of trips per month. It was a growth-stage portfolio company of Anthemis under that firm's Data, Tech and Infrastructure thesis. Kyte was a consumer-facing operator and never published a public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal, and as of this enrichment pass its web properties no longer serve the company.

providers.name: Lumina
providers.description: Lumina (Lumina Innovations) is a San Francisco-based startup building all-electric, autonomous heavy construction equipment. Founded by Ahmed Shubber and Federico Di Palma, the company develops both the hardware and the self-driving software in-house, taking a Tesla/Waymo-style approach to the excavation and earth-moving industry. Its flagship Moonlander ML6 is a 32-ton fully autonomous electric bulldozer with roughly 750 horsepower of peak output and a 414 kWh battery pack. The broader product lineup spans Roadrunner, Moonlander, Bladerunner, and a Powerpack energy system. Lumina does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Luxe
providers.description: Luxe was an on-demand valet parking service that let users request a valet through a mobile app to pick up, park, and return their vehicle, operating in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Luxe is a consumer mobility service with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: Manicube (Elizabeth Arden Red Door)
providers.description: Manicube (Elizabeth Arden Red Door) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Meridianfleetservices
providers.description: Meridian Fleet Services is a holding company that acquires and partners with exceptional fleet service businesses, positioning itself as a permanent home for them. It focuses on preserving each acquired company's legacy and culture while supporting long-term organic growth through stronger teams, better planning and tooling, and scalable operational systems. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirmed a marketing website only (About, FAQs, Contact) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or programmatic surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: mobike
providers.description: Mobike (Chinese 摩拜单车 / 摩拜科技, "Mobike Technology") was a Beijing-based dockless bicycle-sharing company founded in 2015. Riders located, unlocked, and paid for GPS smart-lock bikes through a mobile app and QR codes. Mobike was acquired by Meituan in 2018 and its standalone brand was subsequently folded into Meituan Bike; the public site (www.mobike.com) is now a bare ICP-filing landing page with no developer API, SDK, documentation, or portal surface. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Nanno
providers.description: Nanno was an on-demand babysitting and childcare marketplace startup, founded in 2016 and based in Denver, Colorado, that connected parents with vetted, background-checked sitters through a consumer mobile app (a "childcare on demand" model). Backed by 500 Global among others, the company paused operations at the end of 2021 amid pandemic-driven labor and childcare-market disruption, and its technology and assets were acquired by household-management startup Call Emmy in May 2022. The Nanno corporate entity persists but no longer operates its platform; nanno.com no longer serves a live site. Nanno was a consumer app and never published a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile is retained as a network stub for historical/lineage purposes and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Nizthewiz
providers.description: NizTheWiz Technology Sdn Bhd is a Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia based logistics startup founded in 2015 that operates a crowd-sourced, on-demand same-day local courier and delivery platform. Its consumer mobile app connects senders with a crowd-sourced fleet of couriers and provides live GPS tracking and full last-mile transparency across the delivery lifecycle. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NizTheWiz publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — its product is a consumer-facing courier app rather than a developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Packfleet
providers.description: Packfleet was an all-electric last-mile parcel courier based in London, delivering for hundreds of merchant customers using a zero-emission electric-van fleet with a focus on sustainable, reliable next-day delivery. Backed by Creandum as a venture-funded climate-logistics company, Packfleet wound down its independent brand in March 2025, with its deliveries transitioned to DHL. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published; this profile is retained as a network record. Enriched: no API surface (company now operates as DHL).

providers.name: Parkway Corp
providers.description: A Philadelphia-based real estate and parking infrastructure company that develops, owns, and manages parking facilities and mixed-use properties across the greater Philadelphia region. Parkway operates one of the largest privately held portfolios of urban parking and structured real estate assets in the Mid-Atlantic, providing on-street and off-street parking, monthly parking programs, validation services, and selective property development. The company does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal.

providers.name: Penske
providers.description: A diversified transportation services conglomerate operating truck leasing, logistics, automotive retail, and professional motorsports across North America. Penske Corporation spans Penske Truck Leasing (full-service leasing, rental, and contract maintenance), Penske Logistics (supply chain management, warehousing, distribution, dedicated contract carriage), Penske Automotive Group (retail automotive dealerships in the US, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), and Team Penske (motorsports). The corporate parent has 73,000+ employees and approximately $43B+ in consolidated revenue. Customer self-service is delivered through web and mobile portals (Penske Fleet Insight, Penske Truck Leasing app, Penske Truck Rental); Penske does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal. Penske Automotive Group is the publicly traded subsidiary (NYSE - PAG).

providers.name: Phantom Auto
providers.description: Phantom Auto was a Mountain View, California and Ra'anana, Israel teleoperation company founded in 2017 by Shai Magzimof (CEO) and Elliot Katz (CBO) that built a remote-driving and remote-operation platform letting a human operator monitor and drive a vehicle from thousands of miles away over bonded commercial cellular links. It launched aimed at robotaxis and self-driving trucks as a safety fallback for autonomous vehicles, then pivoted in 2019 to logistics — remotely operated forklifts and yard trucks that have no autonomy of their own, plus autonomous sidewalk delivery robots — and signed customers including Maersk, CJ Logistics, ArcBest and Serve Robotics. It raised roughly $95M in total from Bessemer Venture Partners, Maniv Mobility, InfraBridge and strategic investors ArcBest and ConGlobal, closing a $25M round in 2023, and acquired Swedish low-latency video streaming company Voysys AB in October 2022. Phantom Auto ceased operations on 12 March 2024 after a funding round fell through, laying off its roughly 100-120 remaining employees. The company published no developer portal, public API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest or agent card) while it operated, and its primary host phantom.auto no longer resolves in DNS at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Pluto Mobility
providers.description: Pluto Mobility is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: mobility. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pure Watercraft
providers.description: Pure Watercraft was a Seattle, Washington electric marine propulsion company founded in 2011 by Andy Rebele. It built electric outboard motors marketed as drop-in replacements for 20 to 50 horsepower gas engines, along with lithium-ion battery packs, chargers and Wi-Fi throttle controls, plus a consumer companion mobile app that pulled trip history and telemetry off the outboard over Bluetooth and pushed firmware updates to it. General Motors took a reported 25 percent stake in 2021. The company wound down and sold its assets in 2024, with the outboard line acquired by Raider Outboards and other assets going to a Seattle electric boat club. purewatercraft.com and the former companion-app host app.purewatercraft.com both now 301 to www.pureoutboards.com, the Pure Electric Outboard storefront operated by the acquirer. Pure Watercraft never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its telemetry cloud was private to its own mobile app.

providers.name: Quickshipper
providers.description: QuickShipper is a last-mile delivery and fleet management SaaS platform that helps businesses manage order fulfillment and deliveries. It provides route optimization, order batching, automated or manual dispatching, a courier mobile app, real-time tracking, branded customer notifications, and business analytics. Companies can operate their own fleet or connect with third-party courier providers, and can sync orders automatically through API integration and WooCommerce/WordPress plugins. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Riide
providers.description: Riide manufactures connected electric bicycles combining a street-legal 500W ebike (the Riide 2) with built-in GPS tracking, 4G cellular connectivity, remote lock/disable theft prevention, and a removable battery with state-of-charge monitoring. The company pairs hardware with a mobile app and connected-vehicle services. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass the public site is a consumer product/pre-order page ("coming soon") with no documented developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rimac
providers.description: Rimac Group is a Croatia-based holding company bringing together exclusive hypercars and advanced electrification technology. Its portfolio spans Bugatti Rimac (the hypercar joint venture behind the all-electric Rimac Nevera), Rimac Technology (design, engineering and production of EV components — battery systems, powertrains, battery management systems and electronic control units supplied to OEMs including Porsche, Hyundai, BMW and others), and Verne (autonomous urban mobility / robotaxi). Rimac is a B2B automotive and electrification supplier and vehicle manufacturer; it does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: roxmotor
providers.description: ROX Motor (roxmotor.com) is a Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturer, a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, best known for the ROX 01 electric off-road SUV. It is a consumer automotive brand with no public developer API surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe. The site is hosted on Tencent Cloud and was not reachable from the enrichment environment for content search.

providers.name: Ruedata
providers.description: Ruedata (RueData AI) is an AI predictive tire-management software platform for commercial fleet operators. It combines a smart digital inspection app, the TLGX precision tire-measurement device (tread depth to +/-1/32nd and pressure to +/-0.25 percent), and a centralized web platform to help fleets prevent tire blowouts, cut maintenance costs, extend tire lifecycle, and improve road safety. Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Skip Scooters
providers.description: Skip Scooters (operated by Skip Transport / Waybots) was a San Francisco-based dockless shared electric scooter (micromobility) startup and one of the early operators permitted in San Francisco, also running fleets in Washington, D.C. Backed by Accel, the company wound down and its assets moved to Helbiz around 2020. It is no longer operating: its former consumer app and rider domains (rideskip.com is a parked for-sale domain, skip.com now resolves to an unrelated retailer) have no live developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record; the enrichment pipeline found no public API to harvest.

providers.name: SnapShyft
providers.description: SnapShyft is an on-demand staffing marketplace that connects hospitality, food-and-beverage, and events venues with vetted gig workers for short-notice shifts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (snapshyft.com) serves a coming-soon placeholder page and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, changelog, or /.well-known discovery surface. The only machine-verifiable signal harvested was domain/transport security (TLS 1.3, HSTS, DMARC quarantine); the profile remains a lead awaiting a live developer surface.

providers.name: Spider Fleet
providers.description: Spiderfleet (Spider Fleet) is a Mexico-based intelligent fleet-management platform that helps businesses run and maintain their vehicle fleets. Its public site (spider.com.mx, in Spanish) markets fleet onboarding ("Flotillas"), preventive maintenance scheduling ("mantenimientos"), and quote requests ("cotizacion") for fleet operators, and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a static marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification; two navigation links (contact and login) return 404 and the site's TLS certificate is expired.

providers.name: SpoonRocket
providers.description: SpoonRocket was an on-demand, prepared-meal delivery startup backed by a16z that delivered low-cost ready-to-eat meals on demand. The company has since ceased operations and its spoonrocket.com domain no longer resolves to a live website (AWS Route53 nameservers remain delegated, but there is no A record). It publishes no developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead with no active API to enrich.

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Superpedestrian
providers.description: Superpedestrian was a Cambridge, Massachusetts micromobility company founded in December 2012 by MIT Senseable City Lab co-inventor Assaf Biderman. It built the Copenhagen Wheel electric bicycle retrofit (2017) and then the LINK shared e-scooter fleet (2020), whose differentiator was an onboard Vehicle Intelligence System running self-diagnostic safety checks on every ride. It raised roughly $185M (a $60M round in December 2020 and a $125M Series C in February 2022 with Citi Impact Fund and Sony Innovation Fund) and at its 2022 peak ran shared fleets in about 57 cities across eleven US states and seven European countries. Superpedestrian closed its US operations on 31 December 2023 and auctioned more than 20,000 scooters in January 2024; the European business was sold to Norway's SURF Beyond in February 2024 and subsequently folded into ZEUS Mobility. The company published no public developer program and no machine-readable API contract. Its only known machine-readable surface was per-city GBFS feeds served for host cities at mds.linkyour.city, which are offline. Both superpedestrian.com and link.city are now parked domains that answer HTTP 200 to every path with a domain-parking lander, and link.city is delegated to afternic.com nameservers and listed for sale.

providers.name: TakeWheels
providers.description: TakeWheels (branded "Wheels", operated by Wheels Labs) was a shared electric micromobility platform based in Los Angeles, founded in 2018, that offered seated pedal-assist e-bikes and dockless light electric vehicles for short-distance urban trips. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital, which participated in the company's 2019 Series A. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable developer surface for this company. As of this pass the primary domain (takewheels.com) no longer resolves to the company: it issues a 301 redirect to an unrelated third-party site, indicating the business is defunct and the domain has been repurposed. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no active API surface.

providers.name: Taskty
providers.description: Taskty (تاسكتى) is an Egypt-based online marketplace for on-demand home services, connecting customers with vetted service providers for residential cleaning, furniture and upholstery care, eco-friendly pest control, and home maintenance including plumbing, electrical, painting, carpentry, marble, aluminum, and air-conditioning work. The platform is delivered primarily through consumer iOS and Android mobile apps plus a web presence, with booking, dispatch, and WhatsApp/phone support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Taskty publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Three Wheels United
providers.description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Toyota Connected
providers.description: Toyota Connected is Toyota Motor Corporation's global connected mobility technology arm, building the data, telematics, and software platforms that power Toyota and Lexus connected vehicle services worldwide. The group operates as a federation of regional subsidiaries — TOYOTA Connected Corporation (Japan), Toyota Connected North America (TCNA, Plano, Texas), TOYOTA Connected Europe (TCEU, United Kingdom), TOYOTA Connected India (TCIN), TOYOTA Connected Asia Pacific, and Toyota Tsusho Connected Middle East — and runs Toyota's Mobility Service Platform (MSPF) and the Drivelink telematics backbone behind Safety Connect, Service Connect, Remote Connect, Destination Assist, Wi-Fi Connect, and the "Hey Toyota" in-vehicle voice assistant. TCNA reports surpassing five million connected customer calls across Toyota and Lexus and runs Toyota's Big Data Center for connected-vehicle data. KINTO — Toyota's mobility services brand for car subscription, car-sharing, ride-hailing, and carpooling (KINTO One, KINTO Flex, KINTO Share, KINTO Ride, KINTO Join) — sits adjacent in Toyota's mobility portfolio and is powered by KINTO Technologies on AWS. Toyota exposes developer portals at developer.eig.toyota.com (Toyota API Portal covering TMC, TMNA, TEMA, TFS, NAMC, and other entities) and developer.toyotaconnected.eu (Toyota Connected EU API services, including Telematics and Vehicle APIs documented with Swagger/OpenAPI), but access is gated to partners and internal Toyota teams — no public, unauthenticated OpenAPI specifications are published. Third-party access to Toyota vehicle data for individual developers is typically brokered through partners such as Smartcar and High Mobility rather than directly via Toyota's own portals.

providers.name: TruckLabs
providers.description: TruckLabs built TruckWings, an automated tractor-mounted aerodynamic device that closes the gap between the tractor and trailer to reduce aerodynamic drag, cutting fuel consumption by a proven 3-6% and eliminating roughly 7-10 metric tons of CO2 per truck each year with an 18-24 month payback. The device deploys automatically at highway speed and retracts below it, reduces buffeting and trailer sway in crosswinds, and installs on both new builds and retrofits in about two hours. TruckLabs was acquired by ConMet, and trucklabs.com now redirects to the ConMet TruckWings product line. As a hardware fuel-efficiency company, TruckLabs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Veniam
providers.description: Veniam builds intelligent networking software for the Internet of Moving Things, moving data automatically, securely, and cost-effectively between connected vehicles, mobile IoT devices, and the cloud across all available networks (cellular, Wi-Fi, and DSRC). Its platform serves video telematics, connected fleets, industrial IoT, and auto OEM/Tier 1 use cases, and reports processing 110M+ kilometers of mobile IoT data with 130+ granted patents. Founded by Joao Barros, Susana Sargento, Robin Chase, and Roy Russell, the company was acquired by Nexar in 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. No public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: VR Motion
