providers.description: VR Motion Corp develops virtual-reality driver-training simulation systems, marketed under its RealDrive product, delivering true-to-life driving simulations that the company says achieve over 70% greater skills retention than traditional training. It serves commercial fleets, last-mile delivery operations, first responders, and driving schools. VR Motion is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer API, docs, SDK, or developer portal, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Wonder
providers.description: Wonder is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, bain-capital-ventures, bloomberg-beta, bullpen-capital, forerunner-ventures, general-catalyst, gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zagster
providers.description: Zagster was a venture-funded bike-share startup based in Boston, Massachusetts (a Techstars portfolio company) that designed, built, and operated bike-sharing programs for cities, universities, corporate campuses, hotels, and residential communities across the United States, peaking at more than 200 programs in 2019. The company ceased bike-share operations in June 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic and is now defunct. Its former developer API host (zapi.zagster.com/api/v1/bikeshares) no longer resolves, and zagster.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: BentoBox
providers.description: BentoBox is a restaurant marketing and commerce platform, part of Fiserv, that powers restaurant websites, online ordering, takeout and delivery, events, reservations, and digital presence for thousands of hospitality brands. While BentoBox runs a Technology Partners program and connects to 50+ third-party services across POS, reservations, delivery, payments, marketing, and shipping, it does not publish a public self-service developer API or API reference. Integrations are built through partnership rather than open documentation, and prospective technology partners are directed to contact the BentoBox partnerships team to integrate with the platform. As a Fiserv company, payments and commerce flows connect through Clover and Fiserv rails.

providers.name: Dunzo
providers.description: Dunzo was an Indian hyperlocal delivery and quick-commerce platform founded in July 2014 in Bengaluru by Kabeer Biswas, Ankur Agarwal, Dalvir Suri and Mukund Jha, which grew from a WhatsApp group into an app-based service delivering groceries, food, medicines, pet supplies and same-city packages across up to nine Indian cities. Its Dunzo for Business (D4B) offering gave merchants last-mile delivery through a partner API and through multi-carrier aggregators. Backed by Google, Blume Ventures, Alteria Capital and Reliance Retail, the company was dissolved on 14 January 2025; the app and website were shut down and every Dunzo-operated host, including its merchant API, is now offline. This profile is retained as a historical record — Dunzo publishes no developer portal, documentation, specification or support channel today.

providers.name: NIO
providers.description: NIO is a Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer and technology company that develops smart electric vehicles, battery swap technology, and related autonomous driving and connectivity services. NIO provides developer APIs for vehicle data, energy services, and connected car features.

providers.name: Ofo
providers.description: Ofo (Chinese: 小黄车, "little yellow bike") was a Beijing dockless bicycle-sharing company founded in 2014 by Dai Wei and four classmates from the Peking University cycling club, and launched publicly on 7 September 2015. At its 2017 peak it had deployed more than 10 million bicycles across roughly 250 cities in 20 countries, reported over 60 million monthly active users, and was valued at around US$2 billion; in March 2018 it raised an $866M round led by Alibaba. Ofo's bikes were unlocked exclusively through its own consumer iOS and Android app. The company never operated a developer portal, never published a machine-readable API contract, and never shipped official client SDKs — the only documentation of its endpoints is third-party reverse-engineering of the private mobile-app API at one.ofo.com. Ofo withdrew from most international markets in July 2018, collapsed under a deposit-refund backlog that left more than 10 million users queuing for refunds from December 2018, and had ceased bike-rental operations by 2020. ofo.com is still registered through Alibaba Cloud and still resolves, but its origin refuses connections on ports 80 and 443; the historic ofo.so host dropped and was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2025 and now serves a parked arcade-game lander. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: MisMar
providers.description: MisMar (مسمار) is a Saudi Arabian automotive maintenance and repair platform that connects vehicle owners with certified service centers. It runs a consumer mobile app (B2C) alongside a Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) platform and Workshop Management System (WMS) that digitize fleet management, order processing, and workshop operations for business (B2B), government (B2G), and insurance partners. Services span fault diagnostics, accident restoration, oil and battery and tire changes, periodic maintenance, car wash, and protective treatments across 45+ Saudi cities, with at-home or center-based delivery and warranty coverage. MisMar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is currently published.

providers.name: XING Mobility
providers.description: XING Mobility (行競科技) is a Taiwan-based battery technology company building immersion-cooled lithium battery systems under the IMMERSIO brand, including cell-to-pack (CTP) battery platforms, battery backup units (BBU) for AI data centers, and the automotive-grade XBE energy storage series, serving electric mobility, energy storage (ESS), marine, and data center markets from its Taoyuan City headquarters. A 500 Global portfolio company, XING Mobility publishes no public developer API or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: Bykea
providers.description: Bykea is a Karachi-based Pakistani mobility and logistics super-app that offers app-hailed motorbike rides, on-demand parcel and food delivery, cash pickup and drop-off, and digital payments across major Pakistani cities. It connects a large network of motorbike captains with riders and merchants, positioning itself as a low-cost transport, last-mile logistics, and financial services platform for the mass market. Backed by Prosus Ventures (Naspers), Bykea was added to the API Evangelist network as a mobility-sector portfolio lead; this profile has been enriched with the provider's public security surface (a live RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne bug bounty program) and domain-security posture. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API documentation is exposed - the primary web surface sits behind Cloudflare bot protection.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: RoboDock
providers.description: RoboDock is an autonomous robotics company (Y Combinator W2026) building the robotics layer that powers autonomous EV and AV depots, starting with charging and inspections. Its robots automate depot operations for electric and autonomous vehicle fleets, handling vision-guided plug insertion with verified connection, automated post-trip vehicle inspection, and closed-loop learning that improves efficiency with each charge event. The company targets live EV and AV depots, ports, and logistics yards where charging and core depot operations are still performed manually multiple times per day across mixed fleets. RoboDock is a hardware and robotics business rather than an API provider; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation. Founded by Zinny Weli (CEO, ex-Zipline and Amazon robotics) and Celine Wang (CTO, ex-Plus autonomous systems).

providers.name: TeraWatt Technology
providers.description: TeraWatt Technology Inc. is a next-generation lithium-ion battery company founded in 2020 by Ken Ogata (CEO) and Yifan Tang, headquartered in California with an R&D center in Santa Clara and operations in Japan, including its first mass-production facility in Shizuoka. The company develops, manufactures and commercializes lithium-ion cells engineered for ultra-high energy density, high power output, improved safety and competitive cost, aimed at electric vehicles, drones, eVTOL aircraft and grid-scale energy-storage systems. It closed a Series C round with investors including Khosla Ventures, Temasek, JIC Venture Growth Investments, JBIC, JERA and ITOCHU Technology Ventures. TeraWatt Technology is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public API, developer portal, machine-readable contract or SDK, which was verified by probing its only public host rather than assumed.

providers.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
providers.description: The world's largest automobile manufacturer by production volume, producing a wide range of vehicles from sedans and SUVs to hybrids and hydrogen fuel cell cars. Pioneer of lean manufacturing and hybrid technology through the iconic Prius.

providers.name: OpenEyes Insurance
providers.description: OpenEyes Insurance (OpenEyes Insurance Agency, Inc.) is an Austin, Texas-based insurtech startup, with an additional New York office, that provides commercial auto insurance for truck and bus fleet operators bundled with proprietary risk-prevention technology. Its offering pairs fleet coverage with real-time driver monitoring, AI dashcams, safety analytics, customized driver training, and 24/7 claims management, serving both insurance agents (For Agents) and fleet operators directly (For Fleets). Founded by Yoav Oron (CEO), Dr. Omry Sendik (CTO), and Dan Charash (Chairman), OpenEyes emerged from stealth in February 2023 with a $23M Series A led by Insight Partners with Pitango First. The company operates a customer-facing fleet dashboard but does not publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Bidgely
providers.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

providers.name: Cosmic Robotics
providers.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. Its first market is utility-scale solar energy, with expansion planned into data center construction. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. Cosmic Robotics is currently a hardware and fleet-software company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and any agent-facing surfaces (such as its published llms.txt) as the API Evangelist network enrichment pipeline monitors it for a future API.

providers.name: Enel X
providers.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

providers.name: GM OnStar
providers.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: Sleek EV
providers.description: Sleek EV (SLEEK EV) is a Thai-Singaporean electric motorcycle company founded in 2022, headquartered in Singapore with primary operations in Thailand. Under the mission "Sustainability must be affordable," it builds accessible electric two-wheelers — the TYPE-S, TYPE-E and TYPE-X motorcycles and the SLEEK Play 1.0 urban scooter — powered by its S-DRIVE powertrain and IP67-rated lithium-ion batteries (via Ampace/CATL). It runs the S-Charge fast-charging network (100+ stations across Bangkok) and a SLEEK App for vehicle monitoring, route planning and station finding, sold through a nationwide dealer network. BOI-certified and backed by ORZON Ventures (OR + 500 TukTuks), January Capital, A2D Ventures and Krungsri Finnovate. This is a consumer product company with no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Coreshell
providers.description: Coreshell (Coreshell Technologies, Inc.) is a San Leandro, California battery technology company founded in 2017 that develops silicon-anode lithium-ion battery cells built on low-cost, domestically sourced metallurgical-grade silicon instead of graphite or refined polysilicon. A proprietary nanolayer surface coating stabilizes the silicon anode, and the company has unveiled commercial-scale 60 Ah cells aimed at electric vehicles, defense platforms and stationary energy storage. Coreshell is a materials and cell manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or public code repository.

providers.name: Moment Energy
providers.description: Moment Energy is a Coquitlam, British Columbia clean-energy company that builds battery energy storage systems (BESS) from repurposed electric-vehicle batteries for commercial and industrial customers. Its Luna BESS is described as the first repurposed-battery system to achieve UL 1973, UL 9540, and UL 9540A certifications, and is applied to demand-charge management, grid backup, EV-charging support, and energy arbitrage across data centers, public institutions, transportation, food & beverage, manufacturing, and forestry. Moment Energy is a hardware and energy-services company and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Quantumscape
providers.description: QuantumScape is a battery technology company developing next-generation solid-state lithium-metal batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage. Its anode-free cell design aims to deliver greater energy density, faster charging, longer life, and improved safety versus conventional lithium-ion cells, while simplifying manufacturing and lowering cost. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a corporate website, blog, and investor relations resources but no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Volt14
providers.description: Volt14 Solutions Pte Ltd is a Singapore-based deep-tech startup developing silicon-majority anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Its fully integrated, tunable, and ready-to-use anodes replace conventional graphite to deliver large gains in energy density and lower normalized cell cost, while remaining compatible with existing battery cell manufacturing infrastructure. Target application markets include electric vehicles, consumer electronics, appliances, and power tools. The company is a materials-science and battery-technology producer; it publishes a corporate and careers website but exposes no public developer or API product surface. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: GoTo
providers.description: GoTo (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, IDX: GOTO) is the largest technology group in Indonesia, formed in May 2021 through the merger of the on-demand and ride-hailing pioneer Gojek and the e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. GoTo operates a super-app ecosystem spanning on-demand services (ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, logistics), e-commerce, and financial technology through GoTo Financial (including GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets). The group serves Indonesia's population of more than 270 million, connecting tens of millions of consumers with millions of merchants and driver-partners, and is estimated to contribute roughly 2 percent of Indonesia's GDP. GoTo is backed by a roster of blue-chip investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Alibaba, Google, Tencent, Temasek, and Sequoia Capital India. This company profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Note that GoTo Group's developer surfaces are published per product (Gojek/GoBiz, Tokopedia, GoTo Financial/Midtrans) rather than at a single group-level developer portal; this record profiles the parent holding company.

providers.name: Chery
providers.description: Chery Automobile Co., Ltd. is a Chinese state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui, and one of China's largest passenger-vehicle exporters, conducting business in more than 130 countries and regions. Its brand portfolio spans the core Chery marque (TIGGO and ARRIZO SUV and sedan series), the Fengyun and OMODA/JAECOO new-energy lines, and the QQ city-car brand, with a growing emphasis on the CSH (Chery Super Hybrid) powertrain and connected-vehicle technology. Chery was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As an automotive manufacturer, Chery publishes corporate and consumer web properties but no public developer portal or API surface was found during this pass.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: dstzc
providers.description: dstzc (地上铁, DiShangTie Green Technology, Shenzhen) is a leading Chinese provider of digitalized operations-management solutions for new-energy (electric) logistics vehicles. It operates a full-lifecycle fleet platform covering vehicle sales and leasing, digital fleet management, safety and risk management, maintenance, charging and battery-swap services, and residual-value management, reporting 224,000+ operational vehicles across 3,246 service locations spanning all 333 prefecture-level regions of mainland China. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company has no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hyundai Bluelink
providers.description: Hyundai Bluelink is Hyundai Motor America's connected vehicle service for Hyundai owners, providing remote vehicle control, vehicle status and diagnostics, navigation and route services, safety and security features, and EV-specific charging and climate management. Bluelink is delivered to owners through the MyHyundai with Bluelink mobile app (iOS and Android), the in-vehicle infotainment head unit, the owner web portal at owners.hyundaiusa.com, and connected smart-home and voice integrations (Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, smartwatch apps). Feature sets vary by model year and subscription tier — typically Bluelink, Bluelink+, and Bluelink Connected Care / Remote / Guidance bundles — and include remote start with climate, remote door lock/unlock, remote horn and lights, vehicle finder, stolen vehicle recovery and SVI, automatic collision notification, SOS emergency assistance, monthly vehicle health reports, destination search (powered by Google), in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot (via AT&T on supported models), and EV-specific remote charge start/stop, charge schedule, charge-level monitoring, and pre-conditioning. Bluelink is a consumer-facing, owner-authenticated service. Hyundai does not publish a public developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API keys for third-party integration with Bluelink vehicle endpoints; access is limited to authenticated owners through Hyundai's first-party apps and to enterprise partners under contract (fleet, insurance telematics, charging networks, smart-home platforms). A community ecosystem of reverse-engineered, unofficial Python and Node.js clients (Hyundai-Kia-Connect/hyundai_kia_connect_api, Home Assistant integrations, Bluelinky) is used by enthusiasts and home automation users, but these are not endorsed, supported, or governed by Hyundai and may break at any time.

providers.name: Jinsheng New Energy
providers.description: Guangdong Jinsheng New Energy Co., Ltd. (广东金晟新能源股份有限公司) is a Chinese lithium-battery recycling and materials company headquartered in Zhaoqing, Guangdong, founded in 2010 and originally focused on nickel sulfate production. It operates a closed-loop "urban mine" business: harmless treatment, echelon (second-life) use and hydrometallurgical regeneration of retired lithium-ion batteries into battery-grade nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate, manganese sulfate and lithium carbonate, plus ternary and iron-phosphate precursors and LFP cathode material, and downstream cells for light mobility, commercial and industrial storage, outdoor power stations and solar street lighting. Production is split across Zhaoqing (Gaoyao) in Guangdong and Yichun/Ganzhou in Jiangxi through the wholly owned subsidiary Jiangxi Ruida New Energy Technology, with approved processing capacity of about 204,000 tonnes of spent lithium battery per year. Both the parent and Jiangxi Ruida appear on MIIT's echelon-use and regeneration white lists. The company completed a Series C, is a Hurun and Forbes unicorn-list member, and has pursued a public listing. It is an industrial materials manufacturer and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Ola Electric
providers.description: Ola Electric is an Indian electric-vehicle manufacturer building electric scooters (the S1 family), electric motorcycles (the Roadster line), and home energy solutions (Ola Shakti battery systems), all designed and produced in India around its in-house 4680 Bharat Cell and ferrite-motor technology. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a nationwide Hypercharger fast-charging network and Hyperservice center footprint across India. As a consumer EV and energy hardware manufacturer, Ola Electric publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API reference; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: PurismEV Inc.
providers.description: PurismEV Inc. is an AI-driven electric-vehicle energy optimization platform that processes real-time vehicle data to help fleets, OEMs, leasing companies, and operators reduce energy consumption, extend battery lifespan, and lower operating costs. Its products include Smart Throttle Control technology (range extension), Battery-Aware Smart Charging, a Smart Mobility energy management system (EMS), and a Fleet Management Dashboard for real-time monitoring across cars, delivery trucks, forklifts, scooters, and drones. PurismEV is backed by 500 Global. The company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Resilient Power Systems
providers.description: Resilient Power Systems is a power-electronics hardware company known for solid-state and medium-voltage power distribution and conversion systems, including solid-state transformers for grid, EV fast-charging, and industrial applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass its web presence (resilientpower.com) has moved and now redirects to Eaton, following acquisition; the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other API-consumable surface, so this profile is identity-only. Enrichment probes confirmed the redirect and captured live domain-security posture for the remaining host.

providers.name: SparkCharge
providers.description: SparkCharge operates one of the world's largest off-grid and mobile EV charging networks, delivering on-demand electric vehicle charging to commercial and fleet operators without fixed grid infrastructure. Its offerings span mobile battery-based charging dispatched by technicians, portable off-grid power hubs, and permanent charging installations, serving delivery, rideshare, automotive, ports, and event customers. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: SUNWODA
providers.description: Sunwoda Electronic Co., Ltd. (欣旺达电子股份有限公司, Shenzhen Stock Exchange 300207) is a global lithium-ion battery manufacturer headquartered in Shenzhen, China. Its business spans consumer batteries (smartphone and laptop battery packs), electric-vehicle power batteries, energy-storage systems, energy services, smart hardware, and an innovation ecosystem. Sunwoda supplies battery cells and packs to major consumer-electronics and automotive OEMs worldwide. As a hardware and manufacturing company it operates corporate, investor, supplier (SRM), and bidding platforms, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Tibo Energy
providers.description: Tibo Energy is an Eindhoven-based energy software company building an AI-driven Energy Management System (EMS) for commercial and industrial customers. Its SaaS platform simulates, monitors, and autonomously controls on-site energy hubs and smart grids, coordinating distributed assets such as heat pumps, EV charging stations, and battery storage to cut energy costs and emissions and to unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure without waiting for grid upgrades. Tibo connects hardware through standard protocols such as MODBUS and OCPP via the Tibo Gateway and exchanges data with BMS, SCADA, and ERP systems through open APIs. Since launching in late 2023 it has deployed its EMS across more than 30 industrial sites and is backed by KOMPAS VC, Hitachi Ventures, SET Ventures, WEPA Ventures, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Yassir
providers.description: Yassir is an Algerian-founded super app providing on-demand and financial services across the Maghreb, sub-Saharan Africa, Canada, and France. Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi and headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations centered in Algiers, the company bundles ride-hailing (Yassir Ride), food delivery (Yassir Food), grocery delivery (Yassir Market), and digital financial services (Yassir Cash) into a single consumer mobile app, alongside a Yassir B2B suite covering corporate mobility, meal benefits, procurement, parcel delivery, and digital gift cards. Yassir reports more than six million users, 130,000+ driver and merchant partners, and 4,500 employees operating across cities in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, South Africa, Senegal, Canada, and France. The company has raised roughly $193M to date, including a $150M Series B led by BOND with participation from Y Combinator and DN Capital, and a global sponsorship partnership with Paris Saint-Germain. Yassir is a consumer and merchant-facing super app: it operates iOS and Android apps and a business portal (go-business.yassir.com) but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source project. Driver, courier, restaurant, and store onboarding flow through partner sign-up forms rather than a developer program, and the yassir-tech GitHub organization currently has no public repositories.

providers.name: Vontier
providers.description: Vontier is a global mobility technology company serving convenience stores, fleet operators, and auto repair shops. Its portfolio spans traditional fueling, alternative energy (EV, CNG, RNG), repair tools, and car-wash technology through brands including Gilbarco, DRB, Driivz, Matco Tools, Teletrac Navman, ANGI Energy, and Invenco.

providers.name: Sion Power
providers.description: Sion Power Corporation is a Tucson, Arizona lithium-metal battery developer and manufacturer, spun out of Brookhaven National Laboratory in 1989. Its Licerion platform pairs a protected lithium-metal anode with proprietary electrolyte and cell engineering to deliver rechargeable cells with roughly double the gravimetric energy density of conventional lithium-ion, targeting defense and aerospace systems, uncrewed aircraft, and electrified mobility. The company operates a 115,000-square-foot R&D and pilot manufacturing facility, holds more than 430 international patents and applications, and has raised over $230 million from investors including LG Energy Solution. Sion Power sells physical battery cells under development agreements with OEMs; it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Tractable
providers.description: Tractable is a London-headquartered artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 by Alexandre Dalyac, Razvan Ranca, and Adrien Cohen that applies computer vision and deep learning to automate visual damage assessment for auto and property insurance claims. The platform analyzes photos of vehicles and buildings down to the pixel to produce accident first-notice- of-loss (FNOL) triage decisions, AI-generated preliminary repair estimates, automated claim review for fraud and consistency, subrogation packet analysis, and property repair-cost estimation and underwriting condition assessment. Tractable's flagship offerings include Auto Estimator, Auto Damage Appraiser, Auto Salvage, Property Estimator, Property Underwriter, and the LumaScanner fixed-operations vehicle scanning product. The company serves insurers, dealerships, repair networks, recyclers, and fleet and rental operators including GEICO, Aviva, Mitchell, Tokio Marine, Admiral, Sompo, Aioi Nissay Dowa, and LKQ. Tractable reached unicorn status in June 2021 and secured a $65M investment from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in July 2023, scaling to over 300 employees across offices in London, Warsaw, Paris, Milan, Spain, Romania, New York, Toronto, Tokyo, and Bangkok. The product is delivered through flexible desktop and API integrations with FNOL, estimatics, and claim review systems, but the developer surface is gated to enterprise partners — there is no public developer portal, self-service API key, OpenAPI specification, SDK release, or open-source repository, and no publicly published authentication, endpoint, pricing, or rate-limit documentation.

providers.name: Flock
providers.description: Flock is a London-based commercial motor and fleet insurtech that provides usage-based, data-driven insurance for businesses operating vehicle fleets. Using real-time telematics and data science, Flock prices risk dynamically and rewards safer driving with lower premiums, delivering connected fleet insurance through a digital platform and partner integrations. The company is backed by Anthemis and other investors and operates primarily in the United Kingdom. This API Evangelist profile tracks Flock's public developer and company surface; as of this enrichment pass Flock publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Kobo360
providers.description: Kobo360 is a Nigerian-founded, pan-African B2B digital freight marketplace and logistics technology platform headquartered in Lagos, with operations across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo, Uganda, and other African countries. Founded in 2017 by Obi Ozor and Ife Oyedele II, Kobo360 operates an "Uber for trucks" long-haul logistics model that matches cargo owners and enterprise shippers with truck owners and drivers through a single digital ecosystem. The company runs the Global Logistics Operating System (G-LOS), an enterprise-grade logistics SaaS / digital freight forwarding platform that provides shipper dashboards, end-to-end shipment visibility, driver and truck ratings, embedded credit and working-capital products for carriers, and route and load optimization across the Kobo network of registered drivers and trucks. Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Kobo360 does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open developer portal; integrations with shippers and partners are delivered through enterprise onboarding rather than a self-service API program.

providers.name: Nanogrid
providers.description: Nanogrid was an Oakland, California software startup founded in 2017 by Patrick Sheehan (CEO), Jon McKay (Co-Founder & CPO), and Dan Lopuch (Co-Founder & CTO) that built software to determine the value of residential solar, battery storage, and electric vehicles for homeowners. Its platform simulated, estimated, and optimized these distributed energy resources and captured the operational synergies between the devices. A 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 25 company, Nanogrid raised roughly $150K from 500 Global and Plug and Play Tech Center before being acquired by clean-energy company Arcadia on April 22, 2021. The company no longer operates independently and its nanogrid.tech domain no longer resolves; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record. (Not to be confused with the separate nanoGrid energy-data platform at nanogrid.com.)

providers.name: Amodo
providers.description: Amodo was a European connected-insurance and telematics company founded in Zagreb, Croatia, that helped insurers and brokers build and distribute personalized usage-based insurance (UBI) products. Its Connected Insurance Platform combined a mobile telematics SDK, driver-behavior scoring, customer segmentation, and profiling analytics to power models ranging from try-before-you-buy to pay-as-you-drive and pay-per-mile. Over roughly nine years Amodo ran nearly 50 telematics programs worldwide with insurers including AIG, Porsche Versicherungs, Tower Insurance, and P&V, and was named one of the Financial Times' top five insurtech companies. Backed by Speedinvest, Amodo was acquired by Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT) in March 2023 and folded into CMT's European operations; the amodo.eu domain now redirects to CMT, and the company no longer maintains an independent public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Gigmile
providers.description: Gigmile is an African mobility platform and gig-economy fintech that gives riders, drivers, and fleet operators a pathway to financial independence through affordable vehicle financing and operational support. It offers lease-to-own and flexible financing for motorcycles, tricycles, cars, and electric vehicles (via its Gamma Mobility asset-financing brand), alongside earned-wage access, vehicle insurance, health cover, maintenance, and working-capital/micro-credit for independent gig workers. Founded by Kay and Sam out of Africa's e-commerce sector, Gigmile operates across Nigeria and Ghana (Lagos, Accra) and helps mobility entrepreneurs onboard and scale managed fleets of riders.

providers.name: Estes Energy
providers.description: Estes Energy is a US-based manufacturer of advanced battery packs for heavy-duty transport. Its magnesium-alloy Magnus platform (proprietary MgCarbonit thermo-structural body) delivers roughly 225 Wh/kg for rail, marine, aviation and off-highway applications, with chemistry-agnostic (sodium, LFP, nickel) packs manufactured entirely in the United States. Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: Imara
providers.description: Imara Corporation was a lithium-ion battery technology startup founded in 2006 in Menlo Park, California, that grew out of research at SRI International. It designed and manufactured high-power lithium-ion battery cells and packs based on patented cathode materials science, targeting power tools, outdoor power equipment, hybrid electric vehicles, specialty applications, and power-grid energy storage. Backed by Battery Ventures and Nth Power, it raised roughly $15.65M and reached commercial cell production in 2009 before shutting down around 2010-2011 for lack of manufacturing funding. It is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and is now defunct.

providers.name: Proterra
providers.description: Proterra is a US-based manufacturer of high-energy lithium-ion battery systems for electric vehicles and commercial equipment, including transit buses, trucks, and off-highway EVs, with charging and fleet solutions. Originally an electric transit bus and powertrain manufacturer founded in 2004, the battery-systems business (Powered by Proterra) continues under the proterra.com domain following the 2023 restructuring. It is a physical hardware and energy-storage company backed by Obvious Ventures under its planetary-health thesis, and publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: VLTA
providers.description: VLTA (Volta Charging) is an electric-vehicle charging network that pairs public EV chargers with digital out-of-home advertising displays at retail, grocery, and shopping destinations. The Volta business was acquired by Shell in 2023; its voltacharging.com domain now redirects to Shell's mobility/EV-charging pages, and consumer charging operations are presented under the JOLT brand (joltcharge.com) offering a mobile app to locate chargers, start/stop sessions, and view pricing. No public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or GitHub organization was found during enrichment; this remains an identity/company profile with no API surface.

providers.name: Enevate
providers.description: Enevate Corporation was an Irvine, California battery technology company that developed and licensed silicon-dominant lithium-ion anode and cell technology — marketed as HD-Energy and XFC-Energy — aimed at extreme fast charging (roughly five minutes to a substantial state of charge), high energy density, and cold-weather performance for electric vehicles, with a licensing rather than cell-manufacturing business model. It was a materials and cell-chemistry licensor, not a software vendor, and it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or webhook surface. As of an August 2026 probe the company's own domain no longer serves a company website: enevate.com redirects to a "Website Temporarily Unavailable" domain notice stating the prior Enevate Corporation website has been retired and the domain is now under new ownership following an asset acquisition process, and that all previously published statements about products, services, partnerships and company operations should no longer be considered current. This profile is retained as a recorded absence with the probe evidence attached.

providers.name: Koffie Financial
providers.description: Koffie Financial (originally Koffie Labs) was a New York based insurtech managing general agency selling commercial trucking insurance to fleets, brokers and agents. Founded by co-founder and CEO Ian White and co-founder and COO Michael Dorfman, it paired telematics driven underwriting with digital policy servicing, partnering with Samsara on fleet safety data, Sutton National and Boost on underwriting capacity, and Snapsheet on claims. It raised a 4.5 million dollar seed in 2021 and an 11 million dollar Series A in 2022 led by Anthemis Group, rebranded from Koffie Labs to Koffie Financial, launched the Koffie Card, and was licensed in states including New York, Georgia, Florida and Tennessee. The company never published a public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs; its only machine surfaces were private broker and fleet portals. As of July 2026 its web presence is retired.

providers.name: Fairmatic
providers.description: Fairmatic was a San Francisco commercial-auto insurance MGA founded in 2017 that underwrote and priced fleet policies from phone-collected telematics. It rebranded to LEEO Insurance Services on 2025-12-15, and every Fairmatic-branded web surface now 301/302 redirects to leeoinsurance.com: fairmatic.com and www.fairmatic.com to leeoinsurance.com, docs.fairmatic.com to docs.leeoinsurance.com, app.fairmatic.com to app.leeoinsurance.com. The old API host api.fairmatic.com returns 404 at its root; the live REST Fleet Telematics API is served from api.leeoinsurance.com/api/v1. This repository is therefore a DUPLICATE STUB, created by the harvest backlog from a secondary-market share-listing page rather than from the company's own domain. The canonical, fully enriched profile of this company is all/leeo-insurance-services, which already carries the four OpenAPIs, the authentication, conventions, error, lifecycle, changelog, conformance, data-model, MCP, llms.txt, skills, agentic-access and domain-security artifacts, and the complete Fairmatic-branded SDK line (npm, Maven Central, NuGet, CocoaPods). No artifacts are wired here on purpose: duplicating them would split one company across two listings and two Kin Scores.

providers.name: Lula
providers.description: Lula Technologies, Inc. was a Miami, Florida insurance-infrastructure company founded by twin brothers Matthew Vega-Sanz (CEO) and Michael Vega-Sanz (President). It started as the car-sharing startup Lula Rides and pivoted during the COVID-19 pandemic into an API-first — widely described at the time as "Stripe-like" — insurance platform for small and mid-sized car rental, car-sharing, trucking and logistics fleet operators, bundling driver vetting and risk assessment, fraud detection, driver-history checks, episodic/on-demand policy issuance and claims handling behind a single API underwritten through licensed insurance partners. It raised an $18M Series A in July 2021 and a $35.5M Series B, and its public developer surface was a Postman documenter collection alongside a developer portal at www.lula.is/developers. In 2024 Lula divested its insurance division to Nantucket Capital Corp, a San Diego MGA, headcount fell from roughly 150 to about 19, and the founders sold the company. The domain lula.is has since left the company's control — it now delegates to parkingcrew.net and serves a "This domain may be for sale!" holding page — the API host api.lula.is is gone, and the Postman collection returns 404. No public API surface remains. NOTE FOR FUTURE PASSES — the same founders later built a SEPARATE company, Gail (legal entity Nothing Technologies, Inc., meetgail.com), which does operate a live developer surface; Gail is not a rename of Lula and none of its artifacts may be attributed to this profile. Two other unrelated companies also trade as "Lula": Lula (lula.life, property maintenance) and Lula Commerce (lulacommerce.com, convenience retail). This profile is retained as a historical company record.
